[Eyes of the many headed snake](#note/eyes-of-the-many-headed-snake)

# Description

#### Purpose
Bayard is here to exposition the world, other people are taking an interest in the events around the players. He can become a contact to the city. 

#### Trait: “There Are no Rules and Nobody Looks out for you.”

# Events
- [x] Bayard was sent here to investigate the attacks on traders from [Arendur](#note/arendur). ✅ 2025-06-20
- [x] Someone was feeding lady dagger information about the various convoys leaving Arendur. ✅ 2025-06-20
- [x] He has yet had a chance to find evidence identifying this source, as he does not know where Lady Dagger lives when she is not in these caves. ✅ 2025-06-20
- [x] Bayard is a member of The eyes of many headed snake, his guild was hired to investigate the trader ambushes. ✅ 2022-04-23
- [ ] Bayard does not know that his guild was hired by [Faustus Antili](#note/faustus-antili) of [The Fulcrom](#note/the-fulcrom) spice trader guild.
- [x] Ran into the Shadow Company in the lady dagger caves where he flashed his badge of the guild. ✅ 2022-04-23
- [x] He travelled home to [Arendur](#note/arendur) with [Assumi](#note/assumi-avalande) and [Pinna](#note/pinna) and told [Assumi](#note/assumi-avalande) how to contact him again if need be. ✅ 2025-06-20
- [x] #[Væltepeter](https://app.campaign-logger.com/logs/22172d1943414f6bbaee26c97e55e152/tags/site/v%c3%a6ltepeter) is a place to drink and eat in #[Arendur](https://app.campaign-logger.com/logs/22172d1943414f6bbaee26c97e55e152/tags/site/arendur). ✅ 2025-06-20
- [x] @[Bayard](https://app.campaign-logger.com/logs/22172d1943414f6bbaee26c97e55e152/tags/char/bayard) has mentioned to @[Assumi](https://app.campaign-logger.com/logs/22172d1943414f6bbaee26c97e55e152/tags/char/assumi) that if she wants to get him a message outside of a diplomat pouch, she should go there for a drink and let a red cloth hang from under her mug and leave the message underneath the candlestick holders foot. ✅ 2025-06-20

he reported back to "the eyes"

#### Utility - What to Gain from Bayard

##### Bayard Has Hidden a diplomat’s Pouch in the UmberHulk Pile of Stones Area, He Spent Some time “befriending” it with Gold and Gems. “They Are Surprisingly Enough Appreciative of Valuables, Which is how the Cult Got One to Burrow for Them. They Actually Have intelligence.”

Bayard has heard someone mention old “war stories” of working with a dwarf named [Mellik](#note/mellik) who’s now retired. But will only remember this if PC’s mention [Mellik](#note/mellik). He can get a letter to [Mellik](#note/mellik) with the pouch and through his “handler” and that person he remembers telling stories or get [Mellik](#note/mellik) to write them back.

# His Story for Being in the Lady Dagger Caves
“I’ve been investigating the disappearing merchants on the main road from [Arendur](#note/arendur). Eventually i found that someone called “lady dagger” was running a handful of gangs up and down the road. Took me awhile to get myself inserted in this one, I still havent found out where she lived when she was not with the bandits.” - Jeg har kigget nærmere på overfald af handlende mellem [Arendur](#note/arendur) og grænsen, jeg fandt efter noget tid at nogen der blev kaldt “Lady Dagger” styrede eller koordinerede en håndfuld bandit grupper langs handels ruten. Det tog mig noget tid at infiltrere dem og nå her til. Jeg mangler stadigvæk at finde ud af hvor hun “bor” når hun ikke opholder sig med banditterne.

“Who i work for? Oh i thought… well maybe not everyone is familiar.. Okay, I suppose there is no harm in telling you lot. I work as a spy for Snake eyes, [Eyes of the many headed snake](#note/eyes-of-the-many-headed-snake)? We mostly do work for hire, but we also function as the Thrones intelligence gathering outfit.” - Hvem jeg arbejder for? Øhm jeg troede at… måske skiltet.. Nå men okay, jeg arbejder som spion for “Slangens Øjne” eller “Øjnene af den mange hovedet Slange” også kendt som Medusaerne? Det er hovedsageligt kommisions arbejde, men som de eneste er vi også Tronens Efterretnings organisation. 

“I was looking for a way to get close and alone with Lady Dagger, seemed prudent to get rid of her. Trade was suffering and she’s more than a mere thug, she enjoys it too much i think. There’s something very sinister about her.” - Jeg var igang med at udse mig en måde at komme tæt på Lady Dagger og alene med hende. Hendes bortgang ville være til gavn for [Arendur](#note/arendur)’s handel og så er hun generelt ubehagelig, alt for engageret i vold frem for almen tyveri. Der er noget vederstyggeligt over hende.

# House Varrow of Arendur

House Varrow is aligned with Major House Alvares, Duke Alvares. 

# Emrik Varrow

Late 30's
Middle son 
Sent to serve as bodyguard of House Castilla as a penance for a cousins transgression that he did not stop or report in time.
The punishment was sentenced 10 years ago, and is indeffinent until he is recalled/summoned back to his family.

Part of his training as a young man was initiation into the school of the honed mind, one of the 5 battlemaster schools of Arendur.

Emrik appears observant and cautious, deliberate and thoughtful in his sparse conversation.
Emrik appears methodical in his approach to combat, with precise movements he seemingly thinks three steps ahead. 
He frowns with disdain upon recklessness and punishes this in training with a precise countermove. 
To Emrik, discipline and control are paramount to making conscious intentional combat choices.
Ever is he pointing out situational awareness.

Emrik Varrow is trained in the school of Battlemasters known as The Order of the Methodical Blade, which is noted by the symbol hanging from his belt, a Triangle with an eye in the center.

#### **[The Order of the Methodical Blade](#note/the-order-of-the-methodical-blade)
- **Focus**: Battlefield strategy and tactics.
- **Philosophy**: The Order of the Methodical Blade believes that true mastery of battle is achieved through intellect. Warriors of this order are trained to analyze the battlefield, adapting their tactics to exploit the enemy’s weaknesses and disrupt their plans. Combat is a game of foresight and strategic positioning.
- **Techniques**: Methodical Blade Battlemasters employ a broad range of weapons but rely heavily on tactical maneuvering. They are often the leaders or tacticians in larger battles, where they direct allies and position forces with precision.
- **Symbol**: An eye within a triangle

# Handout Til Frekka

Bodyguard of Lord Davide Castilla, Emrik Varrow. 

Da Frekka træner med Lord Davide's bodyguards og lærer featen at stå bedre fast med sit greatsword, observerer hun at en af de her bodyguard virker meget mere bevidst og kalkuleret med sine bevægelser og handlinger. Han er umiddelbart den af dem der ser ældst ud, måske sidst i 30erne eller på den anden side af 40. 

Emrik Varrow, virker observant, forsigtig, bevidst og betænksom i sine udtalelser og væremåde, en smule reserveret. De andre lader til at se op til ham selv om han ikke virker som om han gør noget som helst for at være nogen form for lederrolle.

Emrik er metodisk i hans tilgang til kamp og med præcise bevægelser lader han til at tænke 3 skridt frem foran sin modstander.
Han har ikke smag for letsindighed og tankeløs kamp, i sin træning af Frekka bliver det straffet med præcise modspil, ofte i samspil med bemærkninger om at skærpe sin situationelle årvågenhed. Emrik sætter disciplin og kontrol meget højt, de er nøglen til bevidste kamp valg imod et beslutsomt mål.

Emrik Varrow er trænet i Battlemaster skolen Den Metodiske Klinge.

   “Every one hundred seasons, the Blood Wood chooses a vessel for its  
vengeance. Ware the one who walks in the Wood’s name.”  
—Phrase found in the tattered journals of the druid Kylak Ironroot  

Nicknames: The Beast of the Dark Wood, Blood of the Underworld, Old Redfang  

Kryx was raised by the Blood Wood in Akacia. Cast out from his gnoll pack as a runt, Kryx wandered the Blood Wood, starving and scared. In a twisted grove of grasping trees dripping black liquid into a pool, an ancient presence embraced him, feeding him dead foliage and filling his veins with the oil of the land.  Able to transform into the twisted visage of a giant hyena, Kryx hunted freely in the woods that embraced him as a dark guardian. During these hunts, Krix met Athlonia in a grove surrounding a long-dead portal to the realm of the unseelie elves. The two saw their connection to the darker side of the natural world and bonded before joining [the charnel house](#note/the-charnel-house).  

Ideal: “From the depths of the earth we rise and  
to depths of the earth we return.”  

Bond: “I smile at the darkness held in the hearts  
of my friends.”  

Flaw: “My hunger for blood and flesh sometimes  
outweighs the better judgment of my companions.”  

Tactics  
In his years traveling with [the charnel house](#note/the-charnel-house), Kryx learned to hold back his initial instinct to shift into his bestial form and tear his enemies limb from limb. Kryx begins combat with his powerful spells before shifting into his fearsome giant hyena form, charging in at spellcasters and less-armored foes.

# Regent Hexton - Political Conspiracy Background

> [!warning]+ GM ONLY - SUPERNATURAL CONSPIRACY
> **HAG BARGAIN**: The supernatural conspiracy (hag deal, newborn sacrifice, goblin protection) is GM-only secret knowledge
> **POLITICAL DETAILS**: Succession questions, bounties, and heir claims are insider/noble knowledge
> **NPC Access**: Political insiders, nobles, and informed parties might know political aspects
> **Player Discovery**: Political elements discoverable through investigation; supernatural elements require major revelation

## Critical Background Information
**Source**: User-provided foundational material from pre-Obsidian campaign notes  
**Status**: Hidden conspiracy connecting current campaign events  
**Relevance**: Explains Hexton's true motivations and supernatural obligations  
**Reveal Status**: Unrevealed plot element for future campaign development  

## The Hag Bargain

### Original Deal
**Hexton's Promise**: To become the new Baron of Bedegaarn Barony  
**Hexton's Payment**: 
1. **Ignore goblin raid reports** - Turn blind eye to supernatural activities
2. **Sacrifice his first newborn** - Personal cost for political power

**Parties Involved**:
- **Regent Hexton** - Ambitious political figure seeking baronial power
- **Green Hag** - Supernatural entity orchestrating the arrangement
- **Elf Woman** - Companion/agent working with the Green Hag

### Deal Fulfillment
✅ **Hexton achieved baronial seat** - Now holds power in Bedegaarn Barony  
⚠️ **Ongoing obligations** - Must continue ignoring goblin activities  
⚠️ **Personal cost** - Obligation regarding his firstborn child  

## Current Political Dilemma

### Image Management Crisis
**The Problem**: Hexton now worries about his public reputation if he continues completely ignoring goblin threats

**His Solution**: 
- **Issue bounties** for goblin raiders
- **Target the Elf Woman** who accompanied the Green Hag during negotiations
- **Justify targeting** - Claims bounties are only for "attack on the baron's keep"
- **Maintain technicality** - Argues this doesn't violate the original deal

### Bounty Specifications
**Targets**:
1. **Goblin raiders** - Public threat requiring response
2. **The Elf Woman** - Direct connection to the hag bargain

**Justification**: Only targeting the specific attack on the baron's keep, not broader goblin activities

## The Hags' Counter-Strategy

### Chaos Orchestration
**Primary Plan**: Use the original baron's heir to destabilize Hexton's rule

#### Strategic Elements
1. **Heir Preservation**: Hags plan for the original baron's heir to be "saved"
2. **Claim Chaos**: Heir's legitimate claim will create political turmoil
3. **Distraction Effect**: Political crisis will divert attention from goblin operations
4. **Military Opportunity**: Heir might muster an army to reclaim the barony
5. **Timing Advantage**: Strike while Hexton is away in [Arendur](#note/arendur)

### Hag Benefits
- **Political chaos** provides supernatural sustenance/power
- **Distracted authorities** allow continued goblin operations
- **Hexton's downfall** potentially releases them from bargain obligations
- **Regional instability** serves broader chaotic agenda

## Campaign Integration

### Current Relevance
**Hexton's Position**: As Regent, he's connected to:
- **[The Shadow Company](#note/the-shadow-company)** opposition (listed as enemy in faction relationships)
- **Baron Hexton's Regime** as established threat
- **Black Lilly Order** (Knight Order controlled by mind-killers under Hexton)

### Political Implications
- **Legitimacy Crisis**: Hexton's rule based on supernatural bargain, not rightful succession
- **Succession Threat**: Original baron's heir represents legitimate claim
- **Supernatural Debt**: Ongoing obligations to hag powers
- **Military Vulnerability**: Forces deployed to [Arendur](#note/arendur), leaving barony exposed

### Faction Relationships Context
**Why [The Shadow Company](#note/the-shadow-company) opposes Hexton**:
- **Illegitimate rule** through supernatural bargain
- **Supernatural corruption** via hag influences
- **Mind-controlled forces** (Black Lilly Order)
- **Threat to regional stability** through chaos orchestration

## Strategic Considerations

### Potential Campaign Developments
1. **Heir's Return**: Original baron's legitimate heir could emerge
2. **Hag Revelation**: Truth about Hexton's bargain could be exposed
3. **Goblin Operations**: Continued supernatural activities under hag protection
4. **Political Coup**: Opportunity to restore legitimate rule
5. **Supernatural Consequences**: Hexton's violation of bargain terms

### Tactical Opportunities
- **Alliance with Heir**: [The Shadow Company](#note/the-shadow-company) could support legitimate claim
- **Expose Corruption**: Reveal Hexton's supernatural bargain
- **Disrupt Hag Plans**: Prevent chaos orchestration
- **Military Timing**: Act while Hexton's forces are in [Arendur](#note/arendur)

## Connection to Current Events

### Red Hand Threat Context
**Hexton's Absence**: Forces committed to [Arendur](#note/arendur) against [red hand horde](#note/red-hand-horde)  
**Barony Vulnerability**: Reduced defenses create opportunity for heir's return  
**Hag Timing**: Supernatural forces coordinate with external threats  

### Shadow Company Opposition
**Legitimate Conflict**: Opposition based on:
- **Rightful governance** vs supernatural usurpation
- **Regional stability** vs orchestrated chaos
- **Military honor** vs mind-controlled forces
- **Political legitimacy** vs hag bargains

## Notes for Future Development
- **Heir's Identity**: Who is the original baron's legitimate heir?
- **Current Location**: Where has the heir been hidden/protected?
- **Hag Powers**: What supernatural abilities support their plans?
- **Goblin Operations**: What specific activities are being protected?
- **Timing Coordination**: How do hag plans align with [red hand horde](#note/red-hand-horde) invasion?

This background explains the deeper corruption behind Hexton's regime and provides multiple plot threads for campaign development, from political intrigue to supernatural horror to legitimacy conflicts.

Ruthless (1/Round). After scoring a critical hit on its turn, the dragon can immediately make one claw attack.

Apperance: coins & gems embedded in hide 
mannerism: blows acid bubbles 
bond: Saarvith will help me restor my hoard, thus i will help him 
flaw: i have a deep fear of the sword that wounded me
## Nature of the Beast
#### Cruel Ambushers

#### Ancient Monuments

#### Life beyond Death
#### Behavior
- Sleeping underwater
- Ranting about the weaklings it has destroyed
- Hiding in ambush
- Vandalizing ancient architecture
- Hiding a portion of its treasure in a secondary lair, just in case; it tries to destroy witnesses
- Flying overhead, hunting
- Wants to complain to someone about the dreariness of its surroundings, and then maybe kill the listener

### Legends and Lore

With an Arcana or History check, characters can learn the following:

DC 10 Black dragons make their lairs in swamps and among the ruins of ancient empires.
DC 15 Black dragons spit acid, and the oldest among them can surround themselves with magical darkness.
DC 20 Obsessed with death, black dragons sometimes extend their existences through an arcane ritual that turns them into liches.

### Black Dragon Encounters

Black dragons live in rotting swamps, lairing among ruins and toppled monuments.

CR 3–4 black dragon wyrmling with 1d4 dragonbound warriors (see warrior), kobolds, or lizardfolk
Treasure 300 gp, 500 sp, 4 sardonyx gemstones (50 gp each), exquisite marble throne (worth 200 gp but bulky), potion of greater healing, leaden helm (acts as ring of mind shielding)

CR 5–10 young black dragon; young black dragon with 1d4 kobolds, shriekers, or stirges; black dragon wyrmling with 1 or 2 dire centipedes, giant scorpions, or will-o’-wisps
Treasure 1,200 gp, 3,000 sp, 2 adamantine-bladed battleaxes (500 gp each), 3 potions of healing, +1 greataxe (named Immortal; the haft is topped with a gold crown)

CR 11–16 young black dragon with banshee, ghost, night hag, or shambling mound 
Treasure 2,000 gp, 5,000 sp, ceremonial gold full plate armor with crowned helm (2,500 gp), potion of superior healing, oil of sharpness, +2 scale armor (the wearer can breathe water)

CR 17–22 adult black dragon; adult black dragon lich; adult black dragon with 2 bugbears, dire centipedes, specters, or will-o’-wisps
Treasure 8,000 gp, 4,000 ep, iron crown set with 25 jet gemstones (100 gp each gemstone), 50 scrolls of lost history and literature (100 gp each), 3 potions of supreme healing, spell scrolls of greater restoration and move earth, carpet of flying

CR 23–30 ancient black dragon; ancient black dragon with mage, otyugh, shambling mound, or wight; ancient black dragon with 2d4 bugbears, lizardfolk, or specters; adult black dragon lich with 1d6 + 4 skeletons and necromancer or ogre mage
Treasure 15,000 gp, miniature replica of city featuring a 3-foot-tall electrum obelisk (5,000 gp), black dragon egg (25,000 gp), potion of speed, 2 arrows of undead slaying, cloak of the bat, crystal ball

CR 31+ black great wyrm; ancient black dragon with 3 banshees or ghosts and 10 or 20 skeletons or zombies; 2 adult black dragons
Treasure 100,000 gp, 2 gem-studded gold crowns (25,000 gp each), 10 pieces of miscellaneous jewelry (2,500 gp each), huge stone calendar that predicts a future catastrophe, 3 potions of supreme healing, mantle of spell resistance, ring of invisibility

### Names
Algarath, Azoth, Ebonflame, Exatharis, Bitterbite, Sear

### Black Dragon Lair Features

The save DC for the following effects is 13 + the dragon’s proficiency modifier. Choose or roll one or more of the following lair features:

- A successful Perception check reveals a hidden
tunnel. If possible, the dragon snaps someone
up in its jaws and squeezes through the tunnel.

- The lair contains craters filled with bubbling
acid. Once per turn, the dragon can use a
legendary action to dunk a grappled creature
into the acid. The creature takes acid damage
equal to one-half the dragon’s breath
weapon damage.

-  Creatures other than the black dragon gain no
benefit from darkvision within the lair. The
dragon can make a creature immune to this
effect by ritualistically scarring it with acid.

### Black Dragon Signs
-  Scorched earth: the black dragon's acidic breath has burned the ground and vegetation, leaving behind a trail of blackened and withered plants.
-  The smell of sulfur: the black dragon's breath has a distinctive sulfurous odor that can be detected from a distance.
-  The sound of hissing: the black dragon's breath makes a hissing sound as it hits the ground and corrodes the terrain.
- Pools of acid: the dragon's breath has formed pools of acidic liquid that can burn and corrode anything it touches.
- Corrupted water: the dragon's presence has contaminated the water in the area, turning it into a dark and murky swamp.
- Withered vegetation: the dragon's acid has killed off most of the plants in the area, leaving behind a desolate and barren landscape.
- The presence of other corrupted creatures: the dragon's presence has corrupted the other creatures in the area, turning them into twisted and malformed monsters.
- The black dragon's lair: the dragon has built its lair near the center of its territory, and it can be seen from a distance as a large, dark cave or ruin.

# Sir Claudio - The Ashtree Knight - Complete Profile

> [!warning]+ GM ONLY - SUPERNATURAL CONSPIRACY
> **FAR REALM PACT**: Claudio has made a pact with "Chok'la Nugrub Anzataloth" - He Who Dreams
> **ABERRANT CORRUPTION**: No longer fully human, transformed by Far Realms patron
> **POLITICAL MISSION**: Currently managing Bedegaarn Barony while Hexton operates in Arendur
> **KNOWLEDGE LEVEL**: Far Realms pact extremely secret, political role publicly known

## Basic Information
**Full Name**: Sir Claudio  
**Title**: The Ashtree Knight  
**Organization**: Knight Order of the Black Lilly  
**Rank**: Knight Retainer to Regent Hexton  
**Military Command**: Ashtree Company (professional soldiers)  
**Current Location**: Bedegaarn Barony  

## The Far Realms Pact

### Patron Entity
**Name**: "Chok'la Nugrub Anzataloth"  
**Title**: He Who Dreams  
**Nature**: Old One/Far Realms entity in aboleth form  
**Manifestation**: Idol housed in basement of Keep of Bedegaarn  

### Pact Details
**Original Followers**: Regent Hexton + 4 Knights (including Claudio)  
**Pact Center**: Worship of the aboleth idol  
**Transformation**: Knights no longer fully human, granted aberrant powers  
**Binding**: Cannot translate sacred tomes without cultist teaching  

### The Fane of Worship
**Location**: Chamber of Stars (Knight Order HQ)  
**Central Focus**: Aboleth-shaped idol of "Chok'la Nugrub Anzataloth"  
**Sacred Texts**: Ancient tomes in untranslatable script  
**Protection**: Far Realms energies counter all magical translation attempts  
**Knowledge Transfer**: Only cultists who made the pact can teach the writings  

## Current Political Mission

### Hexton's Strategy
**Phase 1**: Secure Bedegaarn Barony (COMPLETE)  
**Phase 2**: Infiltrate Arendur political scene (IN PROGRESS)  
**Delegation**: Hexton + 3 knights to Arendur  
**Garrison**: Lady Floret (Moon Knight) + Sir Claudio (Ashtree Knight) maintain barony control  

### Claudio's Responsibilities
**Military Control**: Command Ashtree Company and maintain order  
**Territorial Coverage**: Bedegaarn, Delios, Taernu, Teslions regions  
**Political Authority**: Act as Hexton's representative in barony affairs  
**Supernatural Security**: Protect the Chamber of Stars fane and maintain Far Realms connection  

## The Black Lilly Knight Order Structure

### Complete Knight Roster
1. **Sir Anglim** - The Tear Knight (with Hexton in Arendur)
2. **Lady Floret** - The Moon Knight (remaining in Bedegaarn)  
3. **Lady Morgant** - The Thorn Knight (with Hexton in Arendur)
4. **Sir Claudio** - The Ashtree Knight (remaining in Bedegaarn)

### Transformation from Ironhouse
**Original Identity**: Ironhouse mercenary company  
**Elevation**: Made knight order by Regent Hexton upon seizing barony  
**Enhancement**: Far Realms pact grants supernatural abilities  
**Loyalty**: Bound by aberrant corruption, not traditional feudal oaths  

## Supernatural Abilities

### Far Realms Corruption
**Alien Mind**: Advantage on mental saves against magic  
**Telepathy**: 120 ft. range  
**Aberrant Languages**: Deep Speech, Infernal  
**Psychic Powers**: Innate psionics including charm, suggestion, confusion  
**Entity Bond**: When reduced to 0 HP, controlling mind-killer emerges  

### Combat Capabilities
**Challenge Rating**: 5 (1,800 XP)  
**Armor Class**: 18 (plate)  
**Hit Points**: 90 (12d8 + 36)  
**Primary Weapon**: Frost Brand Greatsword  
**Special Attacks**: Baleful Interdict seals, Psychic Bolt, Infernal Conduit  
**Spellcasting**: 10th-level illrigger with necrotic and charm focus  

## Military Command

### Ashtree Company Composition
**4x Veterans**: Professional soldiers  
**1x Gladiator**: Elite warrior  
**1x Knight**: Lieutenant/second-in-command  
**Command Structure**: Operates as cohesive military unit under Claudio's direct control  

### Operational Area
**Primary Base**: Bedegaarn (Starchamber Keep)  
**Patrol Territory**: 
- Bedegaarn Barony
- Delios region
- Taernu settlements  
- Teslions area
**Mission**: Maintain order, suppress dissent, enforce Hexton's authority  

## Connection to Broader Conspiracy

### Political Layer
**Regional Control**: Securing Bedegaarn as power base  
**Arendur Infiltration**: Supporting Hexton's political maneuvering  
**Legitimacy Questions**: Operating under disputed regency  
**Opposition Forces**: [The Shadow Company](#note/the-shadow-company) and other resistance elements  

### Supernatural Network
**Far Realms Influence**: Spreading aberrant corruption through knight order  
**Cult Operations**: Maintaining worship of "He Who Dreams"  
**Knowledge Preservation**: Protecting untranslatable tomes  
**Entity Communication**: Serving as conduit for patron's will  

### Cosmic Implications
**Unknown Connection**: Potential link to larger Far Realms invasion  
**Reality Threat**: Aberrant influence spreading through political power  
**Divine Opposition**: Possible conflict with other cosmic forces  
**Escalation Risk**: Political success could enable greater supernatural corruption  

## Roleplay Notes

### Personality Under Corruption
**Surface Demeanor**: Professional knight maintaining military bearing  
**Hidden Nature**: Alien thought patterns influenced by Far Realms entity  
**Command Style**: Efficient but unsettling, inhuman precision  
**Loyalty**: Absolute dedication to Hexton and the patron entity  

### Knowledge Limitations
**Public Persona**: Knight serving legitimate regent  
**Hidden Truth**: Aberrant cultist bound to cosmic horror  
**Information Security**: Cannot reveal pact details due to supernatural binding  
**Political Cover**: Uses legitimate authority to mask supernatural activities  

## Campaign Integration

### Current Status
**Location**: Bedegaarn Barony  
**Mission**: Maintain regional control while Hexton operates in Arendur  
**Resources**: Full Ashtree Company + Lady Floret coordination  
**Vulnerability**: Reduced knight presence due to Arendur mission  

### Potential Developments
**Investigation Targets**: Chamber of Stars fane, untranslatable tomes  
**Combat Scenarios**: Confrontation with Shadow Company forces  
**Political Complications**: Legitimacy challenges to Hexton's rule  
**Supernatural Escalation**: Far Realms influence spreading beyond knight order  

### Discovery Possibilities
**Chamber Investigation**: Players could discover aboleth idol in Knight Order HQ  
**Tome Analysis**: Attempts to translate might reveal Far Realms connection  
**Knight Confrontation**: Combat reveals aberrant nature and mind-killer entity  
**Cult Infiltration**: Learning the true nature of the Black Lilly transformation

# THE Necromancer

Hayden Bisset is a merchant from Kvalec who is obsessed with gathering arcane occult power.

He was a member of an occult society for a long time, deeply curious about secrets of the universe. He came across historical documents that mentions  [the sapphiretail staff](#note/the-sapphiretail-staff) [The Staff of Sapphiretail](https://www.notion.so/The-Staff-of-Sapphiretail-4b77c08881df490bb93cbb90a200905e) and since then became super focused on this one item. To him everything else was nick nacks. During his research and investigation he made a pact with an old one and gained knowledge of something known as the [Whisper Skulls](https://www.notion.so/Whisper-Skulls-c3e761adbec44db196611101c61a1a07) that promised him knowledge and power of the undead and he knew of a long dead man who could give him more information of where the Sapphiretail was last known to be.

has been searching for various sources of power over the years, his journal shows a great lust for knowledge of power and little in terms of inhabitions. This was the reason he got into an occult society in Kvalec, it was in this society he found some old documents and read about the Sapphiretail staff.

All other objects of desire seem to fade away once he learned the name of sapphiretail, all his entries after is about his quest to find it. He has scoured libraries, use lots of his merchant fortunes to pay bards for their knowledge, he has sought and bought all manner of books, scrolls and objects from anyone.  Nothing mundane gave him any knowledge. 

At some point he seems to have made a pact with some otherworldly entity he calls Atlach-Nacha, who promised to give him more knowledge. Through his pact he learned of an ancient creation from Tashrans Glory days, the whispers skull and their supposed power of the dead. His notes surmise that if he can gain the power to question the dead, maybe he can find the Tomb of Durso Preiss and ask him where the staff was last seen.

He has been following clues and leads about the whisper skulls and learned one was locked away in an ancient catacomb from an even older empire than Tashran. A secret demon worshipping cult of Orcus had learned of the catacomb, underneath an unknowing monastery and infiltrated the monk order and began doing their secret cult things in the catacombs. Eventually they were discovered and eradicated by The silent sisters. The journal does not go into who they are. He does not mention any dates or years, but it seems to be a long time ago, obscure knowledge people would have forgotten today.

[Journal Hayden Bissets (Prior Thorne)](https://www.notion.so/Journal-Hayden-Bissets-Prior-Thorne-57903e027b9441048a3615f2c40d1f7d)

## NPC Dolist
1. fled  the monastery, across the click claw moors.
2. went to dead mountain, for another clue to [the sapphiretail staff](#note/the-sapphiretail-staff)

# Time a Knight of Axiom
Time  | Image
-------|------------------------------------
 Time is something of the hypocrite among the Inexorables, perfectly happy to speed things up for itself while denying that same ability to anyone else. Many of the Inexorables don't mind if their allies bend the rules so long as their enemies toe the line, and if this seems like commentary on the nature of law and how it tends to be applied, of ocurse it is. Or is it? Mabye it's the opposite. Time enforces the rules of causality and ensures the past remains firmly behind the future in spite of attempts by creatures like the elves to muddy the waters. The Inexorables of Time really doesn't like elves, by the way. The elves have an annoying habit of ignoring causality altogether. |                                                                                 
Tactics: Time prevents enemies from taking bonus actions or reactions, which is very useful for players who want to maneuver around enemies without suffering opportunity attacks. Like most of the knights of Axiom, time lacks ranged weapons and thus is barely effective against flying enemies, but if its target is on the ground, it is going to pummel the thing into oblivioin. Between Haste and Time is Inexorable, Time can act many times, moving around enemies while denying them opportunity attacks, and it can attack seven times! Time prefers to focus on those enemies benefiting from Haste or who act on turns other than their own. And elves, of course.|

vault-of-shadows.title: Vault of Shadows
vault-of-shadows.md:
80ft down clifflike walls, 120ft to the bottom.
Smells of Death
Climb STR DC 12 athletics
Fail dex DC 12 Acrobat
The vault was built many years ago, the craftsman ship looks dwarven, but all writings indicate Worlock and kiri-jolith.
“Ved Kiri-Joliths kraft og Helgen Worlocks autoritet skal denne boks/vault forblive låst. Lad begge deres hellige vrede nedslå enhver der fjerner ondskaben der her er gemt væk fra verdenen.”
“By the power of Kiri-Jolith and the authority of Saint Worlock, this vault shall remain locked. Upon pain of death shall ye not remove what evil is sealed away from the world here.”
The mentions of Worlock and Kiri-jolith are false, to ward of any doo gooders from opening the vault.

## Vault Door

An octagon with 2 other engraved octagon lines inside, it is a double door that now stand ajar slightly, it can be pushed open. At the base of the door, lies a pool of gold. The doors are 6 feet thick, 10 feet wide each and 10 feet tall.

        The gold has been in the engraved octagon lines in the stone doors and was the magical seal keeping the door locked. The magical energies from Erythnul’s punishment for the failed ritual disrupted the magic holding the seal.

        If the door is closed the seal will reform in the grooves of the door, sealing it shut. It will not be opened by KNOCK or any other means than a wish spell. The vault has steel in its walls, as well as the entire vault is unhallowed with the effect of interrupting extradimensional travelling inside.

## Ante Chamber

The first chamber is an octagon shaped chamber, on the western wall is a door similar to the one that was open. This door is sealed and locked with gold filled grooves. The center of the door has a big triangular hole, ca 30cm on each side and a full arms length in depth. The hole is dark and does not go all the way through the door. A wish spell or the triangular key are the only things that can open the door, a wish spell only works for 24 hours after that the door re-seals itself. 

All over the walls and floor are many carvings, octagon patterns in various forms, scattered amongst those are the triangle logo and the artisans makersmark - Duras Kargan 

## Vault Chamber

Another octagon chamber, all the walls are covered in magical runes warding off the chamber from all kinds of scrying, teleporting, passwall etc

        In the center of the chamber is an octagon shaped plateau with another smaller plateau ontop of it. At the top of the plateau is a pedestal, topped with a metal holder upon which is placed a  2½ft long rod, decorated in black and gold and capped with a golden hawks head.

(Rod)History DC 20: A Count von Kempf who tried to rebel and separate his land from the kingdom of Ursia, many ages ago. His family black and gold standard had the words “I do the devil’s work” underneath a hawks head. He amassed great strength of troops before he began claiming he was king of his country and Ursia had no claims or rights or law there. He was publically executed for sedition.

(Count von Kempf) History DC 25  Apparently he had much of the populace with him. There were odd savage rumours about him involving blood drinking. At his execution there was an old woman cursing and spitting shouting things like “he is the land!”. The king donated alot of the counts treasury to the church of __________ (the king knew the truth of count von kempf being a vampire lord and thought it best for the holy powers to guard the evils of belongings. The church had the rod in their possessions until it was lost a few months before Franz betrayed his fellow knights.)

## History of the Vault

The 3 triangles are the symbol of a steel knight who was manipulated and eventually turned to evil. This was during the dragon wars, there are no records that detail exactly what happened, only that he used to be a true honorable goodly knight. He was last seen in the wars wearing black armor and gazing at his enemies with eyes of fire, during the wars he earned the name “Death Knight”. His legend grew and told how he was no longer a living mortal man, but consumed completely by evil.

## The Key

?????????

## History of the Death Knight

(Triangle Symbol) Copper: I have seen this symbol before, briefly in the dragonwars.

History checks - if in a research area like library failure = 1 extra days research pr difference in score DC17 vs Check15 = 5 days research

(death knight) History DC 17: The first mention in Ursia of a death knight was Eric Stoltz, a former steel knight.

(Eric Stoltz)History DC 15: Eric Stoltz was the right hand of a Necromancer the council of three fought and defeated over 200 years ago.

many battles leading up to the full eruption of the Dragonwars. Apparently he was selected among the Steel Knight to be part of a special knight order action directly under Saint Worlock, The Moon Garde Knights.

(the order of moon garde) History DC 20 The order was disbanded during the war and was never heard of again.

(the order of moon garde) Investigation DC 20 - library/church records: There are mentions of a collection of reports regarding the ending of the order, but there was a huge amount of secrecy about them. They were locked away in the library of the Steel Knight Commander.

Secret : After a handful successful operations, the order was felled, by betrayal. Franz Griffin betrayed and murdered his fellow knights. The event was so shameful and embarrassing that many attempts were made to erase it from history. Franz did not return from this event, but a squire survived the incident and could bear wittness under a zone of truth. It is stressed that the zone of truth was not used lightly. Franz led his fellow knights into an ambush, dragonmen attacked and slew them all, by all accounts the Knights had not seen dragonmen before. When the attack was over a dark figure approached and talked with Franz, some deal or agreement was fulfilled and something was returned to Franz. There was mention of a new task, something to do with a dragon heart.

blue-guardians.title: Blue Guardians
blue-guardians.md:
Main: Factions MOC - Arendur
Related: [Assumi](#note/assumi-avalande)

**Faction Identity**: The most prominent wizard guild/school in Arendur, it trains wizards for the academy and selects guild candidates among them. Guild members serve in the city watch. 
**Area of operation**:  Arendur, the city watch, the acaedemy and it also undertakes tasks, missions and jobs anywhere neccesary.
**Power level**: very powerful, has access to lots of magic and wealth. 
**Ideaology**: The blue guardians was originally created to provide the city watch with wizards. Later it has developed into a political might of its own, however it is heavily influenced by which of the Major Houses are in dominant positions within the guild. Besides providing spellcasters to the city watch, they gather arcane lore & knowledge and work to improve their members status in the big city. 

Long-term goals 
- Decrease everyone elses access to magic item by lobbying government for a ban on magic shops - done 
- 
Mid-term goals 
- Restrict access to magic items to people of means  - done 
	- Magic shops must now function as a sort of club with membership fees. - done 
Short-term goals 
- 
# The Organisation
The [Blue Guardians](#note/blue-guardians) is the number one wizard guild in [Arendur](#note/arendur), this is where nobles send their children in hopes of discovering great arcane talents.
They are also nicknamed [The Tower](#note/the-tower) and they reside in the old wizard tower of [Lord Zott](#note/lord-zott), though the top floor is sealed.

**There are 5 ranks in the guild.**
- Ranks 1-2 generally help out the cityguard. 
- Rank 3 either research, experiment or train. 
- Rank 4 are the recruiters 
- Rank 5 are leaders of the guild, of which there are 3. 
- There is a 6th rank, which is the guild master, the residing master of [The Tower](#note/the-tower) who gains benefits from [The Tower](#note/the-tower) as if it was his stronghold. 

[The Tower](#note/the-tower) is a level 4 stronghold.

# Who
Guildmaster
PC handler: [Carlotta Baras](#note/carlotta-baras)

[Google doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oyOEGe5c3GrEJJ70F7M-bbvdttQRK5w-usfwRZuTH2E/edit?usp=sharing)

# Membership
Upon becomming a member of the guild, you write in your name in the guild charter.
Duties of the membership ranks, can be overruled by adventuring as adventuring bands generally provide the realm with safety. However the guild does expect you to come running if they call upon you or your membership is revoked. As an adventurer you are expected to debrief with the guild and share all knowledge learned on your travels. You might even be tasked with gathering specific knowledge.
Each members is marked on the back of their left hand with the guild mark and their rank, with an arcane mark only guild members can see. This mark is placed by a rank 3 or 4 member, the mark also grants access various places in the city.
Maybe Rank 1 = 1st level, Rank 2 = 3rd level, Rank 3 = 5th level, Rank 4 = 7th level, Rank 5 = 9th level?

## Rank 1
Entry level of the guild, you are either tasked with patroling with the city guard or joining an adventurer party. You are also expected to assist teachers in training the apprentices in your downtime as well as assist any of the Rank 3+ with any requests at all. 
Your work in the city guard will usually consist of patroling the most public areas of the city with less troubles.
At Rank 1 you can choose to learn 1 incantation from the following list:

Elemental Aegis
Rank 1 Incantation • Abjuration, Utility (Long)
As a reaction, when an enemy within 50 feet attacks an ally,
choose a damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
Your ally gains resistance to that damage type until the end of
your next turn.
You raise an aegis in your ally’s defense, infusing the shield
with elemental energy to help defend against certain effects

Channeling Shield
Rank 1 Incantation • Abjuration, Utility (Short)
As a reaction, when an attack hits you or an ally you can
see within 50 feet of you, you reduce the damage the target
takes from the triggering attack by 2d10, and the next
successful attack roll you make before the end of your next
turn deals an extra 1d4 force damage.
You throw up a temporary shield to absorb some of the
power of a foe’s attack.
  
Eyes of the Spider Queen
Rank 1 Incantation • Transmutation, Utility (Long)
As a bonus action, for 10 minutes, you gain darkvision out
to 60 feet and can see invisible objects and creatures that are
within 5 feet of you.
A cluster of dull black eyes appears on your forehead,
giving you enhanced sight in darkness and the power to see
the unseen.

## Rank 2:
If you are not an active adventurer, you work in the city guard with more responsibility than rank 1, you oversee important events and are allowed acces in the royal castle. You also work closely with the clerics when there is need for interrogating criminals. You are still expected to assist in [The Tower](#note/the-tower).
At Rank 2 you can choose to learn 1 incantation from the following list:

Chaotic Defense
Rank 2 Incantation • Abjuration, Utility (Long)
As a bonus action, roll a d4 to determine the incantation’s
effect.
1: You gain 3d10 temporary hit points.
2: You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws for 1
minute.
3: For 1 minute, each creature that attacks you takes 2d6
force damage after the attack is resolved.
4: You gain all three of the benefits described above.
You create a din of chaotic sounds, from a wolf’s forlorn
howl to a dead sailor’s dirge. In the cacophony, you find
temporary aid.

Rank 2 Incantation • Abjuration, Utility (Short)

# Hags Mechanics N Stats
## Regional Effects
Green hags may create illusions in the region around their lair to trick and deceive outsiders. Additionally, they may set up noxious traps which they gleefully hope will impede their foes.
• Small bodies of water like ponds in the region have been poisoned. A creature who drinks the poisoned water suffers 4 (1d8) poison damage.
• Corpses within 500 feet of the green hag’s lair become enchanted with illusory magic. They appear to be stunningly beautiful sleeping people.
The illusion fades if the corpse is touched.
• Crows and frogs are more prevalent in the area. 
These effects fade over the course of 1d10 days after the hag is slain.

## Lair Actions
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the hag takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the hag can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row:

• The hag causes a cauldron, pot, or other container of water to bubble up and spew out a noxious, poisonous gas. Each creature within a 10 foot radius must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 9 (2d8) poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn’t poisoned.

• A skull, familiar, or stuffed animal begins to chatter and cackle madly. The closest creature other than the green hag or her allies must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they take 1d4 psychic damage, are deafened and have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of their next turn.

• The hag casts disguise self on herself to look like another creature within 30 feet, then can choose to magically swap places with that creature, or to stay in place.

• Quicksand pits appear in two locations of the Hag’s choice within the lair. 
Each pit fills a 10-foot square and is 10 feet deep. 
When a creature enters the area, it sinks 1d4 + 1 feet into the quicksand and becomes restrained. 
A creature in the quicksand’s area when it appears must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or also start sinking. 
At the start of each of a restrained creature’s turns, it sinks another 1d4 feet. As long as the creature isn’t completely submerged in quicksand, it can escape by using its action and succeeding on a Strength check. 
The DC is 10 plus the number of feet the creature has sunk into the quicksand. A creature that is completely submerged in quicksand can’t breathe. A creature can pull another creature within its reach out of a quicksand pit by using its action and succeeding on a Strength check. 
The DC is 5 plus the number of feet the target creature has sunk into the quicksand.
The quicksand persists for 1 minute or until the hydra uses this lair action again.

- The Green Hag chooses a creature within 30 feet of itself and attempts to bind it with rocks, branches or roots. The creature must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or be restrained until initiative count 20 on the next round. On its turn the druid can cause a restrained creature to sink into the ground and reappear in an unoccupied space on the ground within 60 feet of its starting point. If the druid uses this effect on itself, it is not restrained.

# Ravenscrest Emporium

## About (High-Level Perspective)

Ravenscrest Emporium is an ambitious Royalist merchant network specializing in high-value goods acquisition and no-questions-asked bulk purchasing. They deliberately target growing towns rather than established cities, positioning themselves as an alternative to the dominant Ruby Throne trading network through community investment and fair dealing practices.

---

## History

Founded by **Magnus Blackthorn** as a direct challenge to the Republican-aligned merchant guilds dominating Arendur's trade networks. Unlike traditional merchant operations that focus on major city markets, Ravenscrest developed a strategy of early investment in developing settlements, building community goodwill through civic improvements before establishing permanent trading operations. Their recent expansion into Delios represents their most significant regional operation, carefully timed to coincide with the town's economic growth and Shadow Company presence.

---

## Strategic Framework

### Strategic Imperatives (2-5, Ideally 3)
> [!warning]+ Core Faction Concerns
> These are ongoing, high-level issues that could cause faction collapse if not managed

1. **Avoiding Ruby Throne territorial conflicts**: Must establish market presence without triggering direct trade war with dominant Republican merchant guild
2. **Building community trust and legitimacy**: Success depends on local acceptance despite being outsiders with significant capital
3. **Maintaining operational security**: Their unconventional approach and rapid expansion suggests hidden motivations requiring discretion

### Available Assets
> [!tip]+ Problem-Solving Tools
> Assets determine HOW the faction addresses their strategic imperatives

**Financial Resources**: 
- Substantial capital reserves: Enables 50% bulk purchasing without financing concerns
- Civic investment fund: Sponsors community improvements like Delios bathhouse

**Personnel Network**:
- Magnus Blackthorn (leadership): Strategic mastermind with long-term vision
- Alistair Kingsley (diplomat): Skilled negotiator and community liaison
- Ashley Seidel (operations): Street-level procurement and intelligence gathering

**Business Infrastructure**:
- Flexible procurement model: No-questions-asked bulk purchasing with immediate payment
- Rapid establishment capability: Can set up operations quickly in new territories
- Community goodwill strategy: Civic improvements generate local political support

### Current Strategic Goals

#### **Goal 1: Establish Delios Permanent Operations**
- **Objective**: Complete building renovation and establish sustainable local trading presence
- **Difficulty**: Moderate (4 successes)
- **Assets Deployed**: Financial resources, Alistair's diplomacy, community goodwill
- **Progress**: 2/4 successes
- **Timeline**: Weekly progression checks

#### **Goal 2: Secure Strategic Alliance with Local Powers**
- **Objective**: Formalize relationships with Shadow Company and Delios leadership for market protection
- **Difficulty**: Easy (3 successes)
- **Assets Deployed**: Trading partnership, community investment, political connections
- **Progress**: 1/3 successes
- **Timeline**: Weekly progression checks

---

## Goals & Motivations

**Primary Goal**: Establish alternative Royalist trading network to challenge Republican merchant guild dominance

**Secondary Goals**:
- Build sustainable operations in strategic frontier settlements
- Develop reputation for fair dealing and community investment
- Create intelligence network through merchant activities

**Long-term Vision**: Regional trading confederation loyal to traditional monarchy, providing economic alternative to guild Republican politics

---

## Beliefs & Values

**Core Beliefs**: Traditional monarchy provides stability; merchant guilds should support rather than challenge noble authority
**Alignment**: Lawful Neutral with Royalist political leanings
**Values**: Fair dealing, community investment, long-term relationships over quick profit
**Taboos**: Won't directly challenge local law enforcement; avoids operations that harm established communities

---

## Organization & Members

### Leadership Structure
**Owner/Founder**: **Magnus Blackthorn** - Strategic visionary who remains mysterious; builds network through trusted representatives
**Regional Representative**: **Alistair Kingsley** - Tiefling emissary handling Delios operations with diplomatic skill and business acumen

### Key Members
**Ashley Seidel**: Human female broker handling street-level procurement and local relationship building; represents operational face of organization
**Local Staff**: Small team of clerks, appraisers, and warehouse workers hired locally in each operational area

### Membership
**Size**: Estimated 25-40 personnel across multiple locations
**Requirements**: Business expertise, loyalty to Royalist principles, discretion in operations
**Benefits**: Competitive compensation, travel opportunities, association with growing commercial network

---

## Traits & Behaviors

**Typical Tactics**: Community investment before market penetration; relationship-building over aggressive competition
**Decision-Making Style**: Deliberate and strategic; emphasis on long-term planning and reputation management
**Strengths**: Exceptional capital reserves, flexible business model, strong diplomatic skills
**Weaknesses**: Limited territorial presence, mysterious leadership, potential overextension

---

## PC Integration

### Typical Quests
- **Procurement Missions**: "Locate and secure rare goods for upcoming auction - no questions asked about sources"
- **Market Intelligence**: "Investigate Ruby Throne activities in neighboring settlements to avoid direct conflicts"  
- **Community Relations**: "Assist with civic improvement projects to build local political support"

### Benefits of Alliance/Membership
- Immediate payment for bulk goods at 50% market value regardless of rarity
- Access to rare items through auction network and procurement connections
- Political backing from Royalist network for characters with noble aspirations
- Business opportunities and profit-sharing in merchant ventures

### Requirements from PCs
- Discretion regarding operational details and Magnus Blackthorn's identity
- Preference for actions supporting traditional authority over guild political power
- Respectful treatment of local communities and established relationships

---

## Faction Relationships

> [!important]+ Dashboard Integration Required
> Update YAML frontmatter above with exact faction names for relationship visualization

### Political Alignment
**Stance**: Royalist - supports traditional monarchy and noble authority over guild political power
**Reasoning**: Believes merchant activity should support rather than challenge established noble hierarchy

### Key Relationships

**Allies**: House Worlock (shared Royalist principles and mutual economic interests)
**Enemies**: None currently - deliberately avoids direct confrontation
**Rivals**: The Ruby Throne and The Fulcrom (competing merchant networks with Republican politics)
**Trading Partners**: The Shadow Company (bulk purchasing relationship), Gilded Square (construction materials for civic projects)

---

## Vulnerabilities & Limitations

### Internal Weaknesses
- Heavy dependence on Magnus Blackthorn's mysterious leadership and resources
- Limited operational presence makes them vulnerable to coordinated opposition
- Rapid expansion risks overextending capital and personnel resources

### External Threats
- Ruby Throne could leverage superior resources and political connections to exclude them from markets
- Local authorities might investigate their activities if community goodwill fails
- Economic downturn could eliminate capital reserves needed for bulk purchasing model

### Strategic Vulnerabilities
- Community trust imperative could be exploited through reputation attacks or false flag operations
- Operational security risks exposure if competitors discover their strategic planning or hidden motivations
- Territorial expansion limited by need to avoid direct competition with established powers

---

## Campaign Integration

### Current Status
**Location**: Establishing permanent operations in Delios with renovated building headquarters
**Recent Activities**: Completed Shadow Company bulk purchase, sponsored bathhouse construction, conducting local outreach
**Reputation**: Positive but limited; known for fair dealing and community investment

### Connection to Major Plots
- **Red Hand Invasion**: Potential disruption to trade routes and community stability threatens their business model
- **Political Intrigue**: Royalist stance puts them in opposition to Republican guild networks during political tensions
- **Shadow Company**: Established trading relationship provides mutual support and intelligence sharing opportunities
- **Regional Events**: Delios economic growth and political developments directly affect their expansion success

### Future Development
**Potential Storylines**: Magnus Blackthorn's true identity and motivations; expansion into other frontier settlements; direct confrontation with Ruby Throne interests
**PC Interaction Opportunities**: Rare item procurement, political mediation, protection of trade operations, investigation of competing merchant activities
**Evolution Triggers**: Major economic shifts, political changes favoring Royalists, discovery of hidden agenda, success or failure of Delios operations

---

## GM Implementation

### Weekly Progression
- **Goal Tracking**: Delios establishment (2/4), Alliance building (1/3) - check weekly with advantage when using financial or diplomatic assets
- **Relationship Monitoring**: Track Shadow Company cooperation, local Delios reception, potential Ruby Throne response  
- **Asset Evolution**: Success could grant "Permanent Delios Operations" and "Local Political Influence" assets

### Roleplay Guidelines
**Faction Voice**: Professional, courteous, and community-minded; emphasis on mutual benefit and long-term relationships
**Negotiation Style**: Patient and thorough; willing to invest time and resources for sustainable agreements rather than quick profits
**Response Patterns**: Cooperative with allies, cautious but not hostile toward rivals, generous with communities but protective of operational details

### Integration Notes
**Quest Hook Generation**: Procurement needs create adventure opportunities; community projects require protection; rival activities need investigation
**Political Pressure**: Royalist connections provide alternative to guild-dominated networks; community investment creates local political influence
**Resource Availability**: Immediate gold for bulk goods; access to rare items through auction network; civic improvement funding for allied communities

tax-enforcement-guide.md:
# Tax Enforcement in the Kingdom of Ursia
*Game Master Reference Guide*

## Legal Enforcement Powers

### Property-Based Enforcement
- **Land Confiscation**: Baron can revoke land grants for persistent non-payment
- **Asset Seizure**: Tools, livestock, stored goods taken until debts paid
- **Warehouse Raids**: Tax collectors with guard escort seize untithed resources
- **Business Closure**: Revoking licenses and sealing premises until compliance

### Personal Enforcement
- **Debtor's Prison**: Short-term detention until family/associates pay debts
- **Labor Corvée**: Working off debt through forced labor on public projects
- **Military Impressment**: Conscription as alternative to cash payment
- **Public Stocks**: Humiliation punishment for tax evasion

---

## Escalating Enforcement Procedures

### Stage 1: Administrative Pressure
**Typical Timeline**: 30-60 days after due date
- Official written demands with increasing urgency
- "Penalty" assessments that raise future tax obligations
- Temporary license suspension for businesses
- Blocking access to guild financing or trade partnerships

**DC 12 Persuasion/Intimidation**: Collector convinces cooperation
**Failure**: Escalates to Stage 2

### Stage 2: Social Pressure
**Typical Timeline**: 60-90 days after due date
- Names posted at market squares and temples (public shaming)
- Guild exclusion and professional organization refusal
- Trade embargos from other businesses
- Religious sanctions (priests refuse services)

**DC 15 Persuasion/Deception**: Taxpayer negotiates alternative arrangement
**Failure**: Escalates to Stage 3

### Stage 3: Physical Enforcement
**Typical Timeline**: 90+ days after due date
- Armed guards accompany collectors
- Tax officials occupy defaulter's property
- Mandatory inventory of all assets and production
- Travel restrictions (cannot leave barony)

**DC 18 Intimidation/Investigation**: Enforcement team locates hidden assets
**Success**: Recovery of 50-75% of owed taxes
**Failure**: Escalates to Stage 4

### Stage 4: Severe Sanctions
**Typical Timeline**: 6+ months of resistance
- Land grant revocation and return to Baron's control
- Family and business partner liability extension
- Criminal prosecution for theft from the Crown
- Exile/outlawry (rare, reserved for major cases)

**No skill checks**: Legal process with predetermined outcomes

---

## Regional Enforcement Variations

### Urban Arendur Methods
- **Professional Bureaucracy**: Full-time enforcement officers, detailed records
- **Guild Cooperation**: Professional organizations assist member compliance
- **Formal Court System**: Legal proceedings for disputes and enforcement
- **City Watch Integration**: Guards routinely assist enforcement actions

*Higher success rates but more legal constraints*

### Rural Baronial Methods
- **Personal Relationships**: Collectors know families, use social pressure
- **Seasonal Timing**: Enforcement around harvests when resources available
- **Barter Arrangements**: Accepting goods/services instead of coin
- **Community Pressure**: Village leaders encouraged to enforce compliance

*Lower success rates but more flexible approaches*

---

## Current Campaign Enforcement (648 Z.E.)

### Baron Hexton's Emergency Methods
**Legal Authority**: Questionable emergency wartime powers
**Backing Force**: Black Lilly Knights provide enforcement muscle
**Target Strategy**: Wealthy families who can pay immediately
**Intimidation**: Threatening "sedition" charges for resistance

**Enforcement Modifiers**:
- +3 to Intimidation checks (Black Lilly backing)
- -2 to Persuasion checks (illegitimate authority)
- +5 to Investigation checks (military resources)
- Disadvantage on all checks against Noble Houses

### Current Resistance Patterns
- **Ruby Throne**: Threatening legal challenges in Arendur courts
- **Ranch Families**: Organizing collective resistance and mutual support
- **Local Officials**: Questioning authority for emergency assessments
- **Political Cost**: Each harsh enforcement reduces Baron's legitimacy

---

## Enforcement Personnel

### Official Hierarchy
**Chief Tax Assessor**: Aldric Brennan (coordinates all collection)
**Field Collectors**: Like Jorik (carry documents, conduct assessments)
**Assessment Teams**: Evaluate property and production capacity
**Record Keepers**: Maintain detailed payment and compliance records

### Support Staff
**Guards**: Armed escort for hostile collection areas
**Informants**: Locals reporting hidden production or smuggling
**Appraisers**: Evaluate seized goods and property value
**Bailiffs**: Conduct seizures and public auctions

---

## Creative Enforcement Methods

### Economic Warfare
- **Supply Chain Disruption**: Block access to necessary trade goods
- **Financial Isolation**: Prevent banking and credit access
- **Market Exclusion**: Ban sales at official markets and fairs
- **Resource Control**: Limit access to mills, forges, transportation

### Information Warfare
- **Surveillance Networks**: Monitor production and trade activities
- **Incentivized Reporting**: Reward informants revealing tax evasion
- **Documentation Requirements**: Demand extensive compliance paperwork
- **Audit Threats**: Random "inspections" disrupting business

---

## Taxpayer Resistance Methods

### Legal Resistance
- **Hidden Production**: Conceal actual output before assessment
- **Legal Appeals**: Challenge through proper channels to higher authority
- **Collective Action**: Multiple taxpayers coordinate resistance
- **Documentation Games**: Maintain multiple sets of books

### Criminal Evasion
- **Smuggling Operations**: Move goods through unofficial channels
- **Bribery Networks**: Corrupt collectors to reduce assessments
- **False Partnerships**: Create shell arrangements to confuse ownership
- **Physical Violence**: Armed resistance against collection attempts

**Investigation DCs**:
- Hidden Production: DC 15 Investigation
- False Records: DC 18 Investigation (Insight)
- Smuggling Routes: DC 16 Survival (tracking)
- Bribery Networks: DC 20 Investigation (social)

---

## Enforcement Complications

### Political Constraints
- **Noble Immunity**: Cannot easily enforce against powerful houses
- **Jurisdictional Conflicts**: Overlapping authority between officials
- **Appeal Rights**: Legal processes that delay enforcement
- **Protected Interests**: Some taxpayers have higher authority backing

### Practical Limitations
- **Resource Costs**: Enforcement often costs more than recovered taxes
- **Geographic Challenges**: Remote properties difficult to monitor
- **Seasonal Timing**: Collection limited by agricultural cycles
- **Economic Disruption**: Harsh enforcement reduces future tax base

---

## Adventure Hooks & Scenarios

### Direct Involvement
- PCs hired as enforcement muscle for dangerous collections
- PCs witness tax collector murder, must investigate
- PCs' allies targeted by questionable emergency assessments
- PCs discover evidence of collector corruption

### Indirect Consequences
- Tax rebellion disrupts trade routes PCs use
- Harsh enforcement creates refugees seeking PC help
- Collector discovers PC illegal activities during routine audit
- Political resistance creates opportunities for PC faction advancement

### Investigation Opportunities
- Missing tax collector with evidence of Baron's illegal methods
- Mysterious increase in ranch production (supernatural aid?)
- Smuggling network larger than expected (ties to major conspiracy?)
- Tax records reveal patterns pointing to greater mysteries

---

## Quick Reference Tables

### Enforcement Success Modifiers
| Situation | Modifier |
|-----------|----------|
| Legitimate authority | +2 |
| Armed backup | +3 |
| Community support | +2 |
| Questionable legality | -2 |
| Noble target | -3 |
| Organized resistance | -4 |

### Typical Recovery Rates
| Method | Recovery % | Time Required |
|---------|-----------|---------------|
| Administrative | 85-95% | 1-2 months |
| Social Pressure | 70-85% | 2-4 months |
| Physical Force | 50-75% | 1-6 months |
| Legal Action | 90-100% | 6-12 months |

### Random Complications (d8)
1. Taxpayer has powerful patron's protection
2. Collector accepts bribe, creates false records
3. Enforcement triggers larger political incident
4. Hidden assets discovered during investigation
5. Community organizes collective resistance
6. Religious authority intervenes citing sanctuary
7. Jurisdictional dispute halts proceedings
8. Evidence of collector exceeding authority uncovered

---

*This guide reflects standard practices as of 648 Z.E. Current political tensions may significantly modify enforcement approaches and success rates.*

taxation-system-ursia.title: taxation_system_ursia
taxation-system-ursia.md:
# Taxation System of the Kingdom of Ursia

## Overview
The Kingdom of Ursia operates under a traditional feudal taxation system where land ownership and resource extraction form the primary basis for tax obligations. Unlike modern systems, individual income and personal wealth are generally not subject to taxation. The system is administered through a hierarchy from the Crown down to local Barons.

## Primary Tax Categories

### 1. Royal Land Tribute (The King's Due)
**Purpose**: Fund the Crown, Royal Guards, and central government
**Rate**: 10-15% of assessed land value annually
**Collection**: Local Barons collect and forward to Arendur
**Assessment**: Based on acreage, land quality, and granted privileges
**Records**: Maintained by House Volantis (Royal Treasury administrators)

**Example**: A 500-acre lumber grant might be assessed at 500 gold annual value, requiring 50-75 gold in Royal Tribute.

### 2. Baronial Land Tax (The Lord's Due)
**Purpose**: Fund local administration, infrastructure, and defense
**Rate**: 5-10% of assessed land value annually
**Collection**: Baron's appointed tax collectors
**Flexibility**: Can vary based on local needs and Baron's discretion
**Typical Combined Rate**: 15-25% total (Royal + Baronial)

### 3. Resource Tithes (Production Tax)
**Purpose**: Compensation for use of Crown/Baronial resources
**Method**: Percentage of raw materials extracted
**Common Rates**:
- Timber: 1 in every 10 logs
- Mining: 1 in every 8 loads of ore
- Quarrying: 1 in every 12 stones
- Fishing: 1 in every 15 catches (rivers/lakes only)

**Collection**: Physical delivery to Baron's warehouses or designated collection points

### 4. Trade Tariffs and Market Fees
**Purpose**: Regulate commerce and fund trade infrastructure
**Types**:
- **Border Tariffs**: Goods entering/leaving barony (2-5% of cargo value)
- **Market Fees**: Stall rental and sales permissions (flat daily rates)
- **Export Licenses**: Permission to trade outside the kingdom (annual fees)
- **Guild Fees**: Professional licensing for crafters and merchants

## What Is NOT Taxed

### Individual Commoners
- **No Income Tax**: Workers' wages are not subject to taxation
- **No Personal Property Tax**: Tools, livestock, household goods exempt
- **Alternative Obligations**: Military service, labor corvée, or rent payments to landowners

### Personal Wealth
- **Noble Assets**: Personal treasure, jewelry, weapons not taxed
- **Inheritance**: Wealth transfers freely within families
- **Exception**: Land grants may require Crown approval for inheritance

### Internal Trade
- **Local Commerce**: Sales within a barony typically exempt from additional taxes
- **Barter Systems**: Non-monetary exchanges generally not taxed
- **Personal Use**: Goods produced and consumed by the same household

## Emergency and Special Taxation

### Wartime Levies
**Legal Basis**: Barons may impose temporary additional taxes during genuine emergencies
**Limitations**:
- Must be genuinely temporary (typically one year maximum)
- Cannot exceed 50% increase over standard rates
- Requires formal justification to the Privy Council
- Subject to Crown review and potential reversal

**Common Triggers**: Foreign invasion, natural disasters, major infrastructure needs

### Crown Assessments
**Special Royal Demands**: The King may request additional tribute for specific purposes
**Examples**: Royal weddings, major wars, new construction projects
**Process**: Formal decree through the Privy Council to all Barons

## Administration and Enforcement

### The Collection Hierarchy
1. **Crown Level**: House Volantis oversees royal tribute collection
2. **Ducal Level**: Major Houses coordinate regional collection
3. **Baronial Level**: Local administrators manage day-to-day collection
4. **Village Level**: Town speakers and local officials assist with assessment

### Tax Collector Roles and Powers
**Assessment Authority**: Can inspect lands, buildings, and production facilities
**Record Keeping**: Must maintain detailed records of all collections
**Enforcement Powers**: Can seize property for non-payment (with Baron's approval)
**Limitations**: Cannot enter noble residences without permission

### Common Assessment Methods
**Land Quality**: Fertile farmland taxed higher than rocky or swampy areas
**Resource Access**: Proximity to rivers, forests, or mines affects assessment
**Infrastructure**: Good roads and market access increase taxable value
**Historical Production**: Past yields used to estimate future obligations

## Regional Variations

### Arendur (Urban)
- **Higher Rates**: 20-30% total due to city services and infrastructure
- **Complex System**: Multiple overlapping jurisdictions and guild requirements
- **Professional Administration**: Full-time bureaucrats with detailed records
- **Trade Focus**: Heavy emphasis on tariffs and commercial licensing

### Rural Baronies (Bedegaarn, Dalrath, etc.)
- **Simpler Methods**: Primarily land and resource-based
- **Personal Relationships**: Collectors often know landowners personally
- **Seasonal Collection**: Timed around harvests and major production cycles
- **Greater Flexibility**: More room for negotiation and payment plans

### Border Regions
- **Military Considerations**: Reduced rates in exchange for border defense obligations
- **Trade Routes**: Heavy tariff income from merchant traffic
- **Special Arrangements**: Unique deals based on strategic importance

## Common Tax Avoidance and Disputes

### Legitimate Strategies
**Productivity Claims**: Arguing for lower assessments due to poor yields or conditions
**Infrastructure Investment**: Major improvements can temporarily reduce obligations
**Military Service**: Personal or family military service may reduce tax burden
**Religious Donation**: Large gifts to temples may earn tax considerations

### Suspicious Activities (From Tax Collector Perspective)
**Resource Diversion**: Hiding production before tithes are calculated
**False Partnerships**: Creating shell arrangements to confuse ownership
**Smuggling**: Avoiding tariffs through illegal export routes
**Assessment Fraud**: Misrepresenting land quality or productive capacity

### Common Disputes
**Land Boundaries**: Disagreements over what land is subject to taxation
**Quality Assessment**: Arguments over productive value of holdings
**Emergency Duration**: Challenges to the continuation of wartime levies
**Collection Methods**: Disputes over when and how taxes should be paid

## Current Political Issues (648 Z.E.)

### House Volantis Crisis
- Duke Bartolo Volantis missing, affecting royal tribute collection
- Duchess Elvira refusing to perform duties until husband returns
- King selling Privy Council seats to guilds for immediate revenue
- Old noble families angered by "new money" gaining political power

### Baron Hexton's Irregularities
- Imposing excessive "emergency" levies beyond legal authority
- Selective enforcement favoring political allies
- Using emergency funds for personal political negotiations
- Attempting non-traditional taxation methods (inventory, profit-based)

### Guild Political Pressure
- Ruby Throne and other major guilds challenging traditional feudal taxation
- Demands for representation proportional to economic contribution
- Conflicts between guild commercial interests and noble land rights
- Questions about taxation of purely commercial (non-land-based) enterprises

## Practical Examples

### Ranch Falca Situation
**Standard Obligations**:
- Land Tax: 60 gold annually (500 acres at moderate assessment)
- Timber Tithe: 1 log per 10 cut (delivered to Baron's stockpile)
- Export Tariff: 3% of lumber sold outside Bedegaarn Barony

**Current Problem**: Production increased 50% but tithe deliveries remain static, suggesting either hoarding, smuggling, or some arrangement diverting lumber before official counting.

### The Milly Bell Shop
**Standard Obligations**:
- Business License: 5 gold annually (paid to town)
- Market Stall Fee: 1 silver per market day
- Import Tariff: 2% on goods brought from other baronies

**Why Tax Documents Matter**: As a legitimate business, Millicent would naturally accumulate official correspondence about tax matters, making her shop a logical place for collectors to conduct business.

---

*This document represents the standard taxation system as understood in 648 Z.E. Regional variations and current political changes may affect specific implementations.*

dusty-tome-bookshop.title: Dusty tome - bookshop
dusty-tome-bookshop.md:
"The Dusty Tome" is a renowned bookshop in Delios, run by the son of a retired professor. 

Run and owned by Agusto Lalonde son of Marcio Lalonde a former professor in Arendur 

It has a rich history of acquiring rare and forgotten books from travelers, peddlers, antiquity hunters, and estate cleanouts. 
Its labyrinthine interior houses a diverse collection of ancient tomes, spell scrolls, bestiaries, and journals of legendary adventurers. 
The knowledgeable shopkeeper curates a fascinating inventory, sharing stories and hosting events that attract scholars and adventurers alike. 

It's a treasure trove where one can uncover forgotten secrets and embark on intellectual journeys through the realms.
