# Inventory
1. "Codex Arcanum" - An ancient grimoire filled with forgotten spells and rituals. Price: 200 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to learn the spell "Arcane Preservation" (5th-level, transmutation). [Source: Player's Handbook]
2. "Tales of the Legendary Heroes" - A collection of heroic sagas and epic adventures from across the realms. Price: 75 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC inspiration once per long rest when reading a tale. [Source: Player's Handbook]
3. "The Alchemist's Handbook" - A comprehensive guide to potions, elixirs, and alchemical concoctions. Price: 120 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC a +2 bonus to Intelligence (Alchemy) checks. [Source: Xanathar's Guide to Everything]
4. "Lost Cities of the Forgotten Realms" - A beautifully illustrated exploration of hidden civilizations and ancient ruins. Price: 90 gold pieces. Effect: Provides the PC with proficiency in History (Lost Cities) and advantage on History checks related to lost civilizations. [Source: Dungeon Master's Guide]
5. "Beasts of the Feywild" - A bestiary detailing the fantastical creatures and fey beings of the Feywild realm. Price: 80 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC advantage on Charisma (Nature) checks when interacting with fey creatures. [Source: Monster Manual]
6. "Magical Artifacts and Relics" - A catalog of powerful artifacts with mysterious origins and incredible abilities. Price: 250 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to attune to one additional magical item. [Source: Dungeon Master's Guide]
7. "The Astral Navigator's Guide" - A navigational manual for traversing the astral plane and exploring its celestial wonders. Price: 150 gold pieces. Effect: Provides the PC with knowledge of the spell "Astral Projection" (9th-level, necromancy). [Source: Player's Handbook]
8. "The Enigma of Elemental Magic" - A scholarly treatise on harnessing the elemental forces and mastering elemental spells. Price: 180 gold pieces. Effect: Reduces the spell slot level of all elemental spells cast by the PC by 1. [Source: Elemental Evil Player's Companion]
9. "Chronicles of the Dragonkin" - A historical account chronicling the rise and fall of dragon empires throughout history. Price: 100 gold pieces. Effect: Gives the PC advantage on Intelligence (History) checks related to dragons. [Source: Dungeon Master's Guide]
10. "Secrets of the Shadowfell" - A dark tome unveiling the secrets and dangers of the Shadowfell, a realm of shadows and gloom. Price: 110 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to learn the spell "Shadow Step" (2nd-level, conjuration). [Source: Xanathar's Guide to Everything]
11. "The Bard's Ballads: Melodies of Inspiration" - A collection of enchanting ballads and musical compositions. Price: 70 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC a +2 bonus to Charisma (Performance) checks when performing music. [Source: Player's Handbook]
12. "The Ranger's Guide to Natural Wonders" - A comprehensive guide to flora, fauna, and survival techniques in the wilderness. Price: 85 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC a +2 bonus to Wisdom (Survival) checks in natural environments. [Source: Player's Handbook]
13. "Sorcerer's Spell Compendium" - A compilation of rare and unique spells favored by sorcerers. Price: 120 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to choose one additional sorcerer spell known. [Source: Player's Handbook]
14. "Tales of the Trickster: Legends of Pranks and Mischief" - A collection of humorous and mischievous tales. Price: 60 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC a +2 bonus to Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks for tricks and pranks. [Source: Player's Handbook]
15. "The Warlock's Pact Primer" - A guidebook exploring the different pacts available to warlocks and their associated abilities. Price: 100 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to reassign their warlock pact boon once. [Source: Player's Handbook]
16. "The Paladin's Oathbound Codex" - A holy tome containing sacred oaths and tenets for paladins. Price: 140 gold pieces. Effect: Increases the PC's maximum hit points by 5 when they take their Oath of Devotion. [Source: Player's Handbook]
17. "The Rogue's Handbook of Shadows" - A manual filled with stealth techniques and tricks of the trade for rogues. Price: 90 gold pieces. Effect: Grants the PC a +2 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks in dim light or darkness. [Source: Player's Handbook]
18. "Wizard's Grimoire of Arcane Secrets" - A spellbook containing advanced arcane formulas and theories. Price: 180 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to add two wizard spells to their spellbook. [Source: Player's Handbook]
19. "Monstrous Compendium: Encounters from the Abyss" - A guide to monstrous creatures from the depths of the Abyss. Price: 130 gold pieces. Effect: Gives the PC advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks against fiends. [Source: Monster Manual]
20. "The Divine Hymns: Prayers of Healing and Protection" - A collection of sacred hymns and prayers for clerics. Price: 80 gold pieces. Effect: Allows the PC to add a +2 bonus to Wisdom (Medicine) checks when administering healing. [Source: Player's Handbook]

# Hexton Regent of Bedegaarn

Lord Hexton was the Lord Marshall of Bedegaarn.
He was envious of the power of the baron and believed himself more fit to rule. #secretsnclues 

On a trip he was approached by a woman, offering to read his future and through her card reading he was offered a deal, to claim power for himself. Unlock the keep and let [Sunkiller](#note/sunkiller) and her goblins inside to kill the baron and his family. #secretsnclues 

In return, he must ignore the goblin army and secure the western border. #secretsnclues

in Bedegaarn Barony, close to Teslions. Ruins of an old keep was swallowed up by a giant sinkhole many years ago, remains of it is scattered in a few caverns underground. The sinkhole gorge has been walled up with walls of stone. ?? #develop

dead-mountain.title: Dead Mountain
dead-mountain.md:
A cyclops has taken residence in caves at the top of Dead Mountain.

He is a simple being, set on plunder.

When THE necromancer came across his domain and offered his services to him, he took him up on it. 
[THE necromancer](#note/the-necromancer) created skeletons, zombies and other undeads for the Cyclops, took his payment and went on his way.

There was something in the mountain the necromancer was looking for, the Cyclops had it and traded it for his minions.

Dungeon: Caves of Shadow - main

# Dead Mountain
Main:
Related: [Dead Mountain Attack - Statblock Reference](#note/dead-mountain-attack-statblock-reference)

## Cyclops Necro-Tyrant - CR 8 (3,900 XP) - FINAL BOSS
**AC** 16 | **HP** 138 | **Speed** 30 ft  
**STR** 22 | **DEX** 11 | **CON** 20 | **INT** 8 | **WIS** 6 | **CHA** 10

**Senses** passive Perception 8

**Actions:**
- **Multiattack**: Two slam attacks
- **Slam**: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft, 4d8+6 bludgeoning + 1d6 necrotic damage. On critical hit: target knocked prone, DC 18 Str save or pushed 10 feet
- **Corpse Bolt** (Recharge 5-6): Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 60 ft, 8d6 necrotic damage in 10-foot radius. DC 15 Dex save for half damage
- **Reanimation Command** (Bonus Action): One destroyed undead within sight rises again with 50% HP

**Equipment:**
- **Javelin of Lightning**: +10 to hit, range 30/120 ft, 1d6+6 piercing + 4d6 lightning (10-foot wide line, DC 13 Dex save for half)
- **Amulet of Necromantic Tyranny**: Source of undead control. If destroyed or removed, all controlled undead turn to dust

**Features:**
- **Necrotic Miasma**: 30-foot aura. Creatures starting turn in aura make DC 15 Con save or take 7 (2d6) necrotic damage
- **Poor Depth Perception**: Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets more than 30 feet away

**Tactical Notes:**
- Focuses on controlling undead minions while dealing massive area damage
- Vulnerable if amulet is targeted or removed
- Prefers to hang back and use Corpse Bolt, closes for melee when threatened

haudh-ninlaith.title: Haudh Ninlaith
haudh-ninlaith.md:
Main: [Logged - Session 26](#note/logged-session-26)
# Haudh Ninlaith
*Chapel of the sorrowful lady*

## The Black Eagle Knight
The alexandrian time travel scenario [the black eagle](https://thealexandrian.net/wordpress/38782/roleplaying-games/the-black-eagle)
Alternate version from comments "the claw"

Roadside chapel "haudh Ninlaith" Chapel of [the sorrowful lady](#note/the-sorrowful-lady)

The air smells sad and carries a faint wiff of lavender.

A small mausoleum stands not far from the road, a small trail leads to it. It is overgrown and not very well kept. The entrace has a statue of an elven maid on each side. The interior is one room 20 feet by 20 feet, on the left hand side stands the stone sarcophagus of the lady, on the right side is an empty space. Four braziers held ontop of iron rods (7 feet tall) burns with a soft glow. On the wall opposite the entrace, between the two alcoves hangs the [Tapestry of Grief](#note/tapestry-of-grief).  

The walls are decorated with carvings of vines, trees and foilage. 

In the middle of it all is a 4 feet high stone pillar topped with a metal brazier. 
Religion DC 12: where people can burn offerings while saying a prayer. 

The entire place appears somewhat neglected or cared to by absolute minimal effort.

Stone sarcophagus of the lady, half fey wife of [Duke Armatage Volantis](#note/duke-armatage-volantis) known as The black eagle knight. The Duke died 55 years ago and his wife the lady passed not long after from grief. Being half-fey the family has erected the mausoleum upon their marriage as the lady wished to rest near her ancestors and her husband loved her too much to say no. It is the only Mausoleum of the Volantis family that does not reside inside [Arendur](#note/arendur)

She refused to eat or speak when he died, instead she spent all her time weaving a tapestry. Some say she wove it with her own hair and the day she died was the day she finished the tapestry. The tapestry became known as the [Tapestry of Grief](#note/tapestry-of-grief) and now hangs in the Crypt/Mausoleum.

If the secret elven runes woven into the tapestry is read, Time travel magic is envoked.

An hour after on the road the party will encounter the scene from the tapestry and have a chance to save the knight of the black eagle.

If the savage orcs attacking the black eagle knight is defeated before they can kill the duke, [The Inexorable Time](#note/the-inexorable-time)([ubønhørlige](#note/ubonhorlige))  will appear proclaiming hos causality must be adherred to and will try to kill the Duke and the Characters.

Encounter: [The black oak fight](#note/the-black-oak-fight)

If the party successfully changes the course of time and saves the duke, he thanks them heartily and gives them (one of the characters) a Dukal ring as a sign of his appriciation and says if they ever need something, *"just bring me the ring and your request. With this rings, wherever you go, you go with the blessings of my house."*
Then the black eagle knight and his retinue fade away.

Region complications table could place combats, hazards and ambushes in the rare, very rare with interesting diversions in the common, uncommon.

This can be switched around depending on the type of region. 

In a sparsely civilized region maybe Monster lairs and combat are common and points of interest might be rare or very rare.

A wasteland might have hazards both common and uncommon and anything alive might be rare.

Complications are a great way to express consequences of player actions.

efficient, quiet travel minimizes encounters
slow, loud, reckless, inefficient travel through dangerous terrain increases the odds of wandering monsters thus making them consequences of the travel actions.

The crabs comes from another strange realm.

# Building
The building is not in the best of shape, but it holds up for the most part.
There is a common room with 6 tables, 1 bar, 2 exits: kitchen and backroom.

This is a tavern, a drinking hole, they do not offer rooms.
For room n board they refer you to either [Black portrait Inn](#note/black-portrait-inn) or [Osric's Gold button](#note/osric-s-gold-button), barons and nobles stay at the button, merchants and the like stay at the portrait. det-rustne-baeger.title: Det Rustne bæger
det-rustne-baeger.md:
The Rusty Goblet: A cozy tavern/inn in the heart of Delios known for its friendly atmosphere, 
affordable accommodations, and delicious food. The rustic establishment features a bustling 
tavern area with a well-stocked bar and a spacious dining hall offering hearty meals. Upstairs, 
comfortable and reasonably priced rooms provide a restful stay for weary travelers. 
The inn also has a common room with a fireplace and various amenities for guests to enjoy. 
The staff is welcoming, and additional services such as horse stables and travel assistance are available. 
The Rusty Goblet is a warm haven for travelers seeking comfort and good company in Delios.

Modest lifestyle: 1gp (food, room)
Run by cheerful and boisterous halfling Glimmerleaf Underbottle

**Food Menu:**

1. Roasted Chicken with Herbed Potatoes - Tender roasted chicken served with seasoned herbed potatoes and a side of steamed vegetables. Price: 8 silver pieces.
2. Beef Stew with Fresh Bread - Slow-cooked beef stew simmered with vegetables and aromatic herbs, served with a warm loaf of freshly baked bread. Price: 7 silver pieces.
3. Vegetable Risotto - Creamy Arborio rice cooked with a medley of seasonal vegetables, garnished with grated Parmesan cheese. Price: 6 silver pieces.
4. Fisherman's Catch - Grilled fish fillet served with lemon butter sauce, accompanied by seasoned rice and a side of mixed greens. Price: 9 silver pieces.
5. Shepherd's Pie - A classic dish with layers of savory minced meat, vegetables, and mashed potatoes, baked to golden perfection. Price: 7 silver pieces.
6. Mushroom and Spinach Quiche - A delightful combination of sautéed mushrooms, spinach, and cheese baked in a flaky pastry crust, served with a side salad. Price: 5 silver pieces.

**Beverage Menu:**

1. Ale of the House - A rich and hearty local ale with hints of caramel and a smooth finish. Price: 3 silver pieces.
2. Delios Red Wine - A robust red wine from the nearby vineyards, known for its fruity notes and velvety texture. Price: 4 silver pieces.
3. Elderflower Lemonade - A refreshing blend of elderflower syrup, freshly squeezed lemons, and sparkling water. Price: 2 silver pieces.
4. Spiced Cider - Warm apple cider infused with aromatic spices like cinnamon and cloves, perfect for colder days. Price: 3 silver pieces.
5. Herbal Infusion - A soothing and fragrant blend of locally sourced herbs, known for its calming properties. Price: 2 silver pieces.

# Club Description
The club occupies a grand three-story building constructed from sturdy timber,
adorned with intricate carvings that depict scenes of lumbering and ranching. 
The entrance to Stormpine Hall is marked by a large, ornate wooden door, polished to a rich sheen.

Upon entering, guests find themselves in a welcoming **foyer** that exudes a refined rustic charm. 
The foyer features high ceilings with exposed wooden beams and walls adorned with portraits of the club's founding members, showcasing their accomplishments in the lumber industry. 
A massive stone fireplace dominates one wall, crackling with warmth during colder months.

From the foyer, a grand staircase with a luxuriously carpeted runner ascends to the upper floors, offering access to the various rooms and amenities of the club. On the ground floor, several interconnected spaces cater to different aspects of socialization and relaxation.

To the right of the foyer is the Lounge, a cozy yet expansive area with plush leather armchairs and sofas arranged around low tables. The air carries the scent of aged leather and fine cigars. The Lounge is perfect for engaging conversations, card games, and enjoying drinks served by attentive staff from a well-stocked bar.

To the left of the foyer is the Library, a haven of knowledge and tranquility. Tall bookshelves line the walls, filled with a vast collection of books, scrolls, and tomes on various subjects. Comfy reading chairs and reading lamps invite members to immerse themselves in quiet study or to lose themselves in the pages of adventure and knowledge.

Beyond the Lounge and Library, a wide hallway leads to a large Dining Hall. The hall features long, polished wooden tables with comfortable chairs, capable of accommodating the esteemed members and their guests. Exquisite chandeliers cast a warm glow over the room, while a roaring fireplace at one end adds to the inviting ambiance. Here, delectable meals are served by attentive staff, offering a blend of local delicacies and exotic fare.

Ascending the grand staircase to the second floor, members discover a collection of private rooms and chambers, each tastefully decorated with comfortable furnishings, luxurious amenities, and personalized touches. These rooms provide a retreat for intimate conversations, private meetings, or relaxation.

The third floor houses the prestigious Ballroom, a magnificent space with a vaulted ceiling adorned with intricate wooden carvings depicting scenes of nature and grandeur. The expansive dance floor is flanked by balconies overlooking the room, offering a perfect vantage point for musicians or esteemed guests of honor. The Ballroom is often used for grand celebrations, formal gatherings, and lively entertainment.

Throughout Stormpine Hall, the décor blends the rustic charm of the lumber industry with the sophistication of an elite gentlemen's club. Warm wood tones, elegant furnishings, and carefully curated artwork create an atmosphere of refinement and camaraderie. The club's layout reflects a balance between public spaces for socializing and private areas for contemplation or exclusive events, catering to the needs and preferences of its esteemed members.

1. Foyer: A welcoming entrance area with high ceilings, wooden beams, portraits of founding members, and a grand staircase leading to the upper floors.

### Prompt Players to Go Looking for Things.
Your players probably know, for example, that they need a place to stay. An inn. But maybe they don’t. And maybe they don’t know how to find one. So you tell them. You weave it right into the f{{content}}%ing narration.
Narrate looking for needs: sleep, settle in.
> … and as you drink in the sights and sounds, you realize you need a place to sleep. Should be easy to find a good inn with a little wandering and asking the occasional passerby.

Then, once the characters get settled… talk about selling treasure

> … and now that you've got your things unpacked, you realize you've got a lot of little trinkets to sell. You know it's just a matter of legwork. A few hours wandering the shops and market square will turn all that treasure into gold.

And then… services for equipment, supplies, shopping general adventure items 

> With the gold divvied up, you can replace your supplies and even upgrade your equipment. Shopping around takes a few hours, but you can buy anything listed in PHB. If there’s something special you want, though, talk to me.

> As a cleric, it’s customary to pay your respects to your deity’s local temple and introduce yourself. Maybe even make a donation.
> As a bard, you can probably find out a lot about the town by performing for a few hours and then letting people buy you drinks while you chat them up.

And... Landmarks 
> If you want to know more about that monument, you should consider visiting it. There’s probably a plaque. And the locals there will probably answer questions about it too.

Training facilities in Delios where characters can enhance their skills and abilities.

- Lumberjacks who offer strength training.
- Pit fights in the criminal underground for martial training.
- Drill sessions with the ClickClaw watch or the Shadow Company for martial training.
- A veteran of war who settled in town and offers weapon training.
- Networking opportunities with the Woodriders or a town elder with political experience.
- Izzy the bard who knows many things and can provide networking opportunities.
- Drunken lumberjacks with tales to share for networking opportunities.
- A halfling lass interested in setting up a food place to help the poor offers networking opportunities.
- Hedge wizards or herbalists offering practical training in spellcasting or herbalism.
- Hunters who offer practical training in procuring meat for the town.
- Morgu the carpenter and Mikael the blacksmith offering practical training in their respective trades.
- An alchemist at Ranch Falca offering practical alchemical training. 
- The St. Gaed shrine where a priest offers ritual training.

# Eric Stolz

The original Death Knight of Diamor.

Noone knows exactly how Eric Stolz fell from grace and became the death knight essence. Noone really knows that there is only one death knight, regardless of which fallen knight they face. 

Eric Stolz was among the very first solamnic knights to settle on Diamor. It is believed some demonlord or archdevil managed to sway him to betray his oaths.
	
Eric Stolz can also manifest as THE death knight.

The [council of three](#note/council-of-three) fought and defeated Eric Stolz and a Necromancer over 200 years ago in a small village. 

Dread knights are lesser imitations of Eric Stolz, he has so far failed to create more of his kind.

During the dragonwars Eric Stolz  was petitioned by the cult of dragons to aid them in their efforts. A new knight order was particularly disruptive for them, the moon garde knights. Eric saw the oppertunity to exact revenge on the last remaining member of the [council of three](#note/council-of-three), Worlock.

Eric Stolz having an affinity for sensing corruptible knights managed to corrupt Franz Griffin and with his aid the Moon garde was led into an ambush. Something was given to Franz as payment for this betrayal [Franz Griffins medallion](#note/franz-griffins-medallion)

But even worse was his next mission, the capture and corruption of Thunderclap. 

Eric Stolz empowered **[jawbreaker](#note/jawbreaker)** to earn his nickname, [jawbreaker](#note/jawbreaker) killed Thunderclaps silver dragon mate and one of her horns was imbued with Necrotic power and presented by Franz to Thunderclap before the truth of his betrayal was revealed.

**(death knight) History DC 17:** The first mention in Ursia of a death knight was Eric Stoltz, a former steel knight.

**Eric Stoltz** History DC 15: Eric Stoltz was the right hand of a Necromancer the [council of three](#note/council-of-three) fought and defeated over 200 years ago.

Dragonwars knowledge
**the order of moon garde** History DC 20 The order was disbanded during the war and was never heard of again.

*Investigation checks - if in a research area like library failure = 1 extra days research pr difference in score DC17 vs Check 15 = 5 days research*

**(the order of moon garde) Investigation DC 20 - library/church records**: There are mentions of a collection of reports regarding the ending of the order, but there was a huge amount of secrecy about them. They were locked away in the library of the Steel Knight Commander.

# Locked away Secrets - Steel Knights Archives
**Secret** : After a handful successful operations, the order was felled, by betrayal. Franz Griffin betrayed and murdered his fellow knights. The event was so shameful and embarrassing that many attempts were made to erase it from history. Franz did not return from this event, but a squire survived the incident and could bear wittness under a zone of truth. It is stressed that the zone of truth was not used lightly. Franz led his fellow knights into an ambush, dragonmen attacked and slew them all, by all accounts the Knights had not seen dragonmen before. When the attack was over a dark figure approached and talked with Franz, some deal or agreement was fulfilled and something was returned to Franz. There was mention of a new task, something to do with a dragon heart.

Main: Kingdoms and Empires MOC

Some 1500 years ago give or take, Vampire lords and LichQueens ruled an empire of blood and decadence. They ruled over mortal men as gods.

The nobles and wizards of [Azarumme empire](#note/azarumme-empire) were obsessed with immortality and through the Demon God Orcus they found it in various different ways.

It is as of yet undiscovered how the empire fell, but various evidences of it's existence has been found, investigated and interpreted. The empire's nobility primarily conversed and wrote in Infernal. They were deadly opposed of someone they named The Raven Queen.

They ruled over men, whom they looked upon as cattle and slaves.

They knew many secrets of the dead and some have theorized that the ancient city of Tashran south of Takarnn has it's roots in the Azarumme empire. Believing that some left the empire, either as exiles or maybe an effort to expand the empire, it has yet to be revealed if any theory is correct.

# Dragon's Breath
This tobacco has a fiery kick, with a blend of spices that tickle the senses. It offers a bold and invigorating experience.

typical cost is 20gp for 4 ounce

1. Fireleaf: A rare and fiery plant known for its intense heat and smoky flavor.
2. Dragon's Tongue Herb: A mystical herb that adds a hint of spice and potency to the blend.
3. Emberroot: A root with ember-like properties, giving the tobacco a smoldering effect.
4. Ashenwood Bark: The bark of a special tree that infuses the tobacco with a smoky aroma.
5. Inferno Pepper: A rare and extremely spicy pepper that adds a fiery kick to the blend.
6. Scorched Moss: A type of moss that grows around volcanic regions, lending a unique earthy and smoky flavor.
7. Cinderpetal Flower: A vibrant red flower that releases a burst of heat when burned.
8. Smoldering Embergrain: A special grain that has been charred and adds a smoky undertone to the tobacco.

# Bjælkehytten
  
Før jeg mødte Frekka, ja før jeg havde råd til en hest, vandrede jeg rundt alle steder. Man kan ikke sige jeg nogensinde farede vild, for jeg gik altid bare derhen hvor jeg havde lyst. En dejlig sommerdag med solen højt på himlen og mild og varm vind, kom jeg til en bjælkehytte tæt på en sø. Det var tydeligt at dem der havde bygget hytten havde gjort sig umage – hytten var større og bedre bygget end man ellers ser. Jeg kunne se at hytten så helt forladt ud, som om ingen havde boet der længe, men indenfor stod alting urørt og jeg fik en fornemmelse at at jeg hellere måtte sove udenfor, hvis nu familien der boede i hytten alligevel skulle komme tilbage lige netop den aften. 

Jeg lavede et lille bål tæt på søen, slog lejr og ristede pølser over ilden. Så spiste jeg mine pølser imens solen gik ned og jeg nød at have fundet dette smukke lille sted.

Pludseligt kom der en lyd fra min side. Jeg drejede hovedet og så et væsen der var lidt højere end mig, med grøn våd hud og lange vandplanter hængende fra dets krop og lemmer, helt indsmurt i mudder. Det lignede at det havde ligget på bunden af søen i lang tid.  Væsnets øjne lyste rødt og i dets hånd holdt det hvad der lignede en kort stav af vand, der lyste med et magisk grønt skær. Væsnet slog med staven ud efter mig og i det øjeblik mærkede jeg en fornemmelse af Deja-vu, imens verden omkring gik i stå.

Jeg kunne se et væld af grene, ligesom et lyn der forgrener sig ud i mange veje. Lige nu ville væsnet ramme mig med vand staven, og jeg kunne se min skæbnetråd ende et kort stykke længere ude af den forgrening. Men deja-vu’et var der – en anden tråd i blandt tusinder men en af få hvor staven ikke ramte og hvor min livstråd fortsatte længere væk, udenfor synsvidde. Uden tid til at tænke over det og med frygten sugende i maven hev jeg den korte tråd til mig med den ene hånd og med den anden greb jeg Deja-vu’et  og satte det der hvor den korte tråd før var. 

Verden fortsatte nu pludselig og i det sekund gik det op for mig at der stod endnu tre grønne væsner bag ved den med staven. En anden lidt mindre end den første og to der var meget mindre. Alle stirrede med lysende røde øjne og var kun få øjeblikke fra at nå hen til mig.

Imens staven ramte hvislende forbi, genkaldt jeg den nye formular jeg lige havde lært, men aldrig havde brugt før. Magien susede ud fra mine fingre, og da ildkuglen ramte alt foran mig, blev den grønne vand stav omdannet til grønligt damp og forsvandt. Så snart staven blev ødelagt så jeg små tegn på at de fire væsners grønne farve og røde lys i øjnene forsvandt en smule. Så ramte ilden dem og de faldt forvredne og brændende om i den bløde jord, tæt på søen.

Jeg ville ønske jeg kunne have reddet dem. Jeg tænker tit på om de kunne være blevet reddet på en eller anden måde. I stedet var det eneste jeg kunne give dem, et gravsted ved siden af deres hytte. 

Måske, en dag om lang tid når mine vandringer er forbi. Når jeg har opnået noget. Noget som kan retfærdiggøre at jeg skulle leve, imens de skulle dø. Fordi jeg ændrede skæbnen. Så vil jeg tage tilbage til den fine bjælkehytte, tæt på den smukke sø. Jeg ved lige hvor den er, og jeg glemmer det aldrig.

-Anton Keene

# Sheet

# Who
Frekka Flammehår, a female half-elf from a babarian tribe in Akacia.

# Background
Frekka er eneste barn af Erakki Magnusdatter af Ståløkse stammen, en nomade stamme som følger Urcia Okserne rundt i landet. Hendes ophav var hemmelig for hende, indtil få dage før hendes moder døde, hvor Erakki fortalte Frekka at hendes fader var en ude fra stammen. Derfor var Erakki og Frekka tidligt i hendes barndom, blevet forvist fra stammen. Urent blod med dem fra de civiliseret lande var en uhelligheds som trodsede de Ældres regler. Det faldt derfor på Erakkis skuldre at lære den unge Frekka op. Som årene gik, sygnede moderen mere og mere ind og brugte mere og mere tid på at rejse i ånde verdenen, end på Frekka. Det bekymrede ikke Frekka til at starte med. Hun havde tidlige fundet en ven, en [Siofrah - Rød Talende Panda](#note/siofrah-rod-talende-panda) som kom til hende når hun var helt alene. Sammen startede et venskab som skulle vare indtil at Frekka's mor gik bort. En aften hvor Frekka kom hjem fra en særdeles hård jagt, lå moderen på hendes dødsleje. I febervildelse nævnede hun et ord som den dag i dag, Frekka ikke kan forstå. Da Frekka satte sig på knæ ved hendes moders side, kiggede Erakki op på hende og med en langsom hvisken, forbandede den dag at Frekka blev født. Den unge kvinde sad lamslået tilbage da moderens sidste åndedrav forlod hendes tynde krop. Sådan sad hun indtil den næste morgen. Med indtåret tåre på sine kinder, rejste hun sig op, greb "Brumynda" - hendes sværd som var opkaldt efter navnet en gammel kriger legende, og drog bort. Hun efterlod sig sit mor og alt andet og gik imod et nyt liv.

# Relations
- Mother, shunned from the tribe for giving birth to a elf bastard.
- Siofrah red panda 

# Motivation
- Prove my worth
- Satisfy wanderlust

# Knowledge

# Frekka & Anton Travel Knowledge
Main:
Related: [Frekka Flammehår](#note/frekka-flammehar), [Anton Keene](#note/anton-keene)

## White Tusk Clan
A clan of orcs in the mountains between Ursia & Akacia has got themselves a new leader who is more cunning and sophisticated than other Orc bloodchiefs. These orcs plot and scheme, their leader Bonebreaker Dorokor is a crafty and strategic warrior whose might is often mentioned by the other orcs. [The white tusk tribe](#note/the-white-tusk-tribe) has been known to negotiate, but not above taking what they want.

Latest news is that Bonebreaker Dorokor is paying for information about something called The Sanguineous Oriflamme. Her trusted right hand Oregg Steeltwister even left her side to go looking for clues in Ursia.

## Takaarn Merchants
Takaarn merchants are using the 200 year truce to make money, they frequently travel to Ursia and Akacia with goods from the great Karakurum (The eastern coast of Takaarn, where the great Khan city also lies.)

## Points of Interrest
### Magic Workshop
You've heard rumours of a noble sponsoring a magic workshop up in the southeast mountains in Ursia. Some wizard managed to convince him to sponsor his research with promises of profit.

### Taernu
Taernu was besieged by wolf riders, a stone giant and a fire breathing flying monster.

### Teslions
You met a some survivors fleeing Teslions from the east, the town was evacuated under threat of a goblin horde set on sacking it. Most left for [Arendur](#note/arendur) to the north. The town council was forewarned by a group who called themselves The Shadow company. 

### Baron Hexton
The old Baron was killed when an elven witch invaded Bedegar keep with her goblin minions and slaugthered the whole family. Lord Hexton, a good friend of the Baron stepped up and took over and kept order in the barony. While order is maintained, it is done so by force and hard discipline. Passing through Bedegaarn a forthnight ago you heard that the Baron is cracking down hard on the criminals, especially the Thieves guild "The Clock". But who can argue with being at odds with criminals?
	The Baron has granted knight titles to a former band of mercenaries and formed a new knightly order The black lilly knights. They number 4 knights, The Moon knight, The Tear knight, The Thorn knight (nickname blackrose by the commoners), The Ashtree knight. Of these The Thorn Knight is the most feared and loathed, The Moon knight a close second. The Ashtree knight is the most respected, but still feared, he is rumoured to be the most just of them all. The Black Lilly knights are extensions of the Baron's will, where they travel they are judge, jury and most of them also the executioner.
The Baron has been mustering units for his Army for some time.

### Blackwood
The [blackwood](#note/blackwood) is home to many dark things, if rumours, gossip and old wives tales are to be believed. Over the last 3 years the area around Blackspear ruins has turned into a swamp, rumours persist of a dragon living there. Some dragons could possibly twist the landscape with their presence, maybe there is truth to those rumours.

the-ritual-of-promotion-in-the-shadow-co.md:
# Promotion Ritual of the Shadow Company
The ritual shall take place inside a circle of blades, one blade for each of the last 5 officers that has gone before. 
Their names written in the chronicle, shall be inscribed on the blades. 

The captain of the company shall stand in the circle, with the promotee, reading from the chronicle.

Krøniken fortæller os ikke hvor kompagniet kommer fra, men den fortæller os at kompagniet igennem tiden har stået for broderskabt og forenelse.
Kompagniet har stået fast i storme, vandret i skyggerne og ikke givet op overfor det ukendte. Krøniken bærer vidne til kompagniets, vores, gerninger, eftermæle så ingen af os glemmes.
Vores navne står skrevet med blod, dem der kom før os hviler i bogen som også vi skal hvile der når det er vores tid.
Sammen er det vor tid til at skrive historien, med blod og loyalitet.
Lad os stå forenet i denne cirkel af stål, hylde dem der kom før, hædre dem som står her nu.
Hvor andre kun vandre i solen, skal vi ikke frygte skyggerne, lad andre frygte vores skygger.

1.  Then the captain recites the [Oath of Brotherhood - Shadow company promotion Ritual](#note/oath-of-brotherhood-shadow-company-promotion-ritual)  
2.  He recites the promotee's accomplishments, strengths, and encouragement for their new role.
3.  He instructs the promotee to don the tabard and repeat the [Oath of Brotherhood - Shadow company promotion Ritual](#note/oath-of-brotherhood-shadow-company-promotion-ritual) 
4.  He states the virtues, values and principles of the company, ending with emphasiz on unity and loyalty
5. All gathered shall acknowledge the new officer by proclaiming the company MOTTO

*(Below features triggers after having spent time training with your units)*

**Master at arms**
Learn a Fighting style of your choice

**Soldiering**
Any roll to influence soldiers, guards and other organized martial forces, made by you or made by an ally in your prescense gains advantage.  (gm's discretion). 

**Combat Manuevering**
Your speed increases by 10 feet

**"Reposition!"** Prof.bonsu/long rest
Use a bonus action to call for a tactical withdrawl, you and all allies who can hear you can immediately use a reaction to take the disengage action and move full speed. The Master at arms, do not use a reaction to disengage and move.

**"Shake it off!"**  Prof.bonus/long rest
Use your reaction to give an ally that you can see and that can hear you one of the following effect: 
- reroll a failed save, must use the new roll.
- reduce dmg taken from one source by 2d8+prof
- immediately make an ability check to break free of restrained condition, as opposed to your next turn. (gm's discretion)

## Chaplain, Tactician, Soul and Courage of the Company - Brumor - Steffen
*(Below features triggers after having spent time training with your units)*
Having a chaplain appointed grants a morale boost to the entire organization, as long as his inspirering rituals and cermons are performed on a regular basis. 

In battle, the Chaplain can dedicate their turn to reciting inspiring war litanies, benefiting a specific number of allies (determined by their proficiency bonus plus charisma modifier) within a 60-foot range who can hear them. These allies receive the effects of Bless and Heroism without requiring concentration. This ability persists until the end of the fight and can be used a number of times per day equal to the Chaplain's proficiency bonus. Please note that the Chaplain is unable to use bonus actions or reactions while performing this.

- **Bless**: Targets gain a d4 to attack rolls and saving throws.
- **Heroism**: Targets gain temporary hit points at the start of each turn and become immune to most things causing the frightened condition.

# Battle Magic

Some commanders gain access to battle magic, allowing them to create magic items designed for war that can be distributed among the units they control. Only one item can be used on a commander’s turn. These items are limited use, and expend their magic either immediately or at the end of the battle. Each martial advantage creates a single item per battle.

Whenever a unit is affected by an opposed unit’s battle magic, in addition to resolving the other effects of the magic, that unit must succeed on a DC 13 Morale test or suffer 1 casualty.

Wands. Wands must be given to artillery or aerial units during deployment. A magic wand belongs to the specific unit it is given to, and can be used every round.

Scrolls. Magic scrolls are single-use items. They are not assigned to any specific unit at deployment, but can be assigned to any unit by its commander at any time.

a-domain-organization.title: A Domain-Organization
a-domain-organization.md:
# A Domain-Organization
Main:
Related: [Organisations MCDM - what is it](#note/organisations-mcdm-what-is-it)

# Domains

Every fantasy RPG campaign contains domains. The local church is one. The baron, their court, and the people of the barony are another. The thieves’ guild. The secret society of rangers and druids. Whatever your choice of fantasy subgenre, your campaign contains many different domains feeding a network of alliances, allegiances, suspicions, and grudges.

The rules in this book give you a straightforward way to represent those domains with game mechanics, and to allow the player characters to step up onto a larger stage and translate their influence from adventuring into political power. Player-run domains are called organizations. NPC-run domains are called realms. This book presents eight different player organizations, each with three specialties, and another sixteen NPC realms.

When two domains come into direct conflict, this is called an intrigue. The purpose of intrigue is to move toward a climactic confrontation involving combat between the officers of opposed domains and battles between their armies. Some adventures might end with just a final warfare battle at the end of intrigue, while others will feature numerous smaller battles leading up to a final battle alongside a final combat between the characters and the officers of an opposed domain. A domain can be destroyed only by neutralizing its officers. As such, once an intrigue starts, it continues until initiative is called for the final showdown between the domains’ officers.

In simplest terms, the rules in this book assume that characters continue adventuring as they normally do. While the characters are adventuring, slowly working their way toward a final confrontation with the villain, their domain is looking for allies to lend aid, investigating the villain and their lieutenants to learn their secrets, and disrupting the workings of the villain’s realm to weaken that realm’s forces in a final showdown.

a straightforward adventure can include rewards such as military units or resistance to an opposing realm’s features based on a domain’s actions during the adventure.

A character can be an officer in more than one organization, but they can be involved only in one intrigue at a time and can benefit only from the

effects of one party sheet at a time. (That’s the record of a domain’s stats, defenses, and features.) A wizard might be a member of the party’s noble court organization and run their own arcane order on the side. But during an intrigue involving the noble court, the character is focused on that organization while their arcane order tends to its own affairs.

## What is an Organization?

An organization is a domain built around the officers who founded it—the player characters. The players decide what their characters’ organization does, and who its initial allies and enemies are. Among those allies, an organization also includes the NPC followers, retainers, and lieutenants the characters attract as a result of rising fame or infamy earned through adventuring. For example, if the party’s organization is an underworld syndicate, that organization includes all the members of the syndicate down to the lowest-level agents keeping their ears to the ground and feeding the characters information. Likewise, an organization set up as a noble court might include large numbers of farmers and laborers who rely on the heroes for protection, and who are ready to serve to show their thanks.

Using the rules in this book, an adventuring party becomes an organization when it founds a stronghold, typically by buying, building, discovering, or inheriting it. Founding a stronghold announces to the world that the adventurers are more than just mercenaries, and are ready to get involved with local affairs in one way or another.

A domain has four skills: Diplomacy, Espionage, Lore, and Operations, each of which has a modifier. A domain’s officers use these skills during intrigue.

A domain has three defenses: Communications, Resolve, and Resources. Each defense has a numerical value that provides a target number for tests made with domain skills during an intrigue. Each defense also has a level that can be raised or lowered. Any domains can gain bonuses or take penalties during battle or combat based on their domain defense levels.

Each domain also grants its officers access to special domain powers they can use in combat. Each officer gets a power die that they roll at the beginning of any combat against one or more officers of an opposed domain. The roll goes into a power pool shared by all the officers of a domain, with these dice fueling each character’s domain powers.

Every domain also provides a number of unique domain features that officers can make use of during intrigue, allowing the domain to affect the opposed domain’s defenses and units, to muster special units, and make other preparations for battle.

Finally, each domain has a size that determines how many turns it can take during intrigue, how large its officers’ power dice are, and the scope of certain benefits available to the domain’s army

### Founding, Stronghold
Once the characters gain a stronghold, they naturally start to attract followers. Folks hear about the deeds they’ve done, notice the new headquarters, and volunteer to help or serve the characters. That stronghold and those followers are the foundation of the player characters’ organization.

### Titles

Each character can only benefit from one title at a time, but can have multiple titles as well as be part of multiple organizations. 

Optional rule: GM may decide to not use title's and their powers if the party is not a single-class party.

### Points, Boxes, and Bonuses

Each organisation's party sheet defines the starting stats of the Organization's skills and defenses. These can be increased with Development points.

These are spent on boxes on a development track pr skill and defense. 

Start: 8 points 
Domain level up: 8 points

domain-intrigue.title: Domain Intrigue
domain-intrigue.md:
# Domain Intrigue
Main:
Related: [Organisations MCDM - what is it](#note/organisations-mcdm-what-is-it)

# Intrigue

Conflict between domains is called intrigue, and serves as the backdrop to the warfare battles that can play out between the heroes and the villains. The characters can use their organization’s skills outside of intrigue, making use of Diplomacy to forge alliances, Espionage to gather intelligence, and so forth. But once the heroes decide it’s time to act and stop the villain (or once the villain decides to stop the heroes), the GM announces that intrigue has begun as its own special phase of the game.

Intrigue occurs between two domains—by default, the heroes’ organization and the villain’s enemy realm. NPC realms might also be involved, but they don’t act on their own during intrigue. Rather, they lend aid to one side or the other.

Intrigue is divided up into domain turns, during which the players and the GM make use of the domain features and special actions available to them. Intrigue ends once both sides have completed all their domain turns, at which point the GM will set up a final showdown between domains— involving combat between the characters and their enemies, a climactic battle between the armies of powerful domains, or both!

Initiating Intrigue 

the GM determines when intrigue begins, regardless of which side initiates it.

Before intrigue begins, the characters’ organization can probe and test their enemy, **but they can’t use their skills directly against a villainous realm.** That kind of action is what begins intrigue. This is a fine line, and it’s up to the GM to adjudicate it. 

But in general, if the characters can make use of their organization’s skills to deal with everyday people (for example, learning something about a villainous realm by making general inquiries using Diplomacy) or known information (for example, researching a villain’s history using Lore), then those activities can remain part of the regular game. 

A Diplomacy test made against one of Lord Sas allies might provide some idea what kind of army he’s preparing without starting intrigue. But an Espionage test to spy on Lord Sas would initiate intrigue. 

Likewise, a Lore test to learn what Lord Sas can do in combat might be allowable outside of intrigue if the GM decides Lord Sas has shown off his combat skills often enough that there are people outside his domain who know that information. But any domain skill that requires targeting a villainous realm (including its agents, libraries, and lands) should start intrigue.

Domain Skill Tests

A domain skill test works exactly like a character or creature making an ability check. A d20 is rolled, modifiers are added, and the total is compared to the test’s Difficulty Class, determined by the GM. If the total is equal to or higher than the DC, the test succeeds.

For example, a Diplomacy test—along with some good roleplaying and effort on the characters’ part—could change the attitude of a clan of elves toward an organization, so that once intrigue begins, the DC to convince the elves to aid the organization is lower.

Outside of their place in intrigue, there are no hard and fast rules describing how domain skills can be used. Players can suggest ideas, and if the GM agrees that an idea makes sense, they can try it! The goal with skills outside of intrigue is to keep the rules purposefully broad, so each table can develop their own standards.

How long it takes to resolve a domain skill test outside of intrigue is also up to the GM.

Regardless of how the GM rules, characters use their domain’s skills by giving orders to the organization’s followers and waiting, sometimes for days or even weeks of campaign time. During that time, those followers work to carry out those orders. Making an Espionage test to determine what military units a villainous realm has mustered can take an enormous amount of effort to pull off, including long days spent in research and networking.

During intrigue, the players can use their organization’s skills to put their army together, or sabotage certain elements of the opposed domain’s power structure to impose penalties on its skills or defenses. At the same time, agents of the villainous realm are making their own attempts to weaken the characters’ organization.

As a rule, the heroes’ organization can’t research or confront a villainous realm they don’t know about, or which is beyond the reach of their influence. The characters can’t use their friendly neighborhood thieves’ guild to sabotage another domain on the other side of the planet.

During an intrigue, each domain can act a number of times equal to 4 + the domain’s size. Each time a domain acts during an intrigue is called a domain turn. This is true for the heroes’ organization as well as the villain’s realm.

Choosing Actions

During a domain turn, the characters’ organization and the villainous realm act at the same time. The GM chooses a domain action for the villainous realm and keeps it secret. Then the characters choose a domain action for their organization. After the players declare the organization’s domain action, the GM reveals the action of the villainous realm. Once actions are declared, the players roll any necessary skill tests for their characters’ organization’s domain action while the GM does the same for the villainous realm. Then the players share the results of their organization’s actions followed by the GM sharing the villainous realm’s results.

Enemies know when units are mustered or when a domain’s stats are improved, but knowing which units a domain has or what the domain’s current stats are requires a successful Espionage test.

When a domain takes a turn, **one** of its player character or NPC officers **runs the domain turn**, directing the domain to make use of its domain features, or to use domain skills as a domain action. Many features also involve the use of domain skills. When using a domain skill, if the officer is proficient with any of the domain skill’s associated character skills, they can add their proficiency bonus to the skill test roll. However, this can be done only once per officer per intrigue.

There are three domain action types: **domain action, domain bonus action, and domain reaction**. An officer can make one domain bonus action in addition to a domain action during a domain turn. Each officer can take **only one domain reaction during an entire intrigue**. Any domain reactions that an officer can make have specific triggers noted in their descriptions

When domain turns happen is up to the GM, once pr week, once pr day, once pr combat encounter, once pr short rest, twice whenever xp is awarded or any other way. They can also change during an intrigue. The final domain turn usually occurs just before the climactic confrontation in battle begins.

domain-units.title: Domain Units
domain-units.md:
# Domain Units
Main:
Related: [Organisations MCDM - what is it](#note/organisations-mcdm-what-is-it)

## Units

Each unit in the organization must be controlled by an officer of the organization. Each Officer can command a number of units equal to their proficiency bonus. 

During the Intrigue, players can muster more units. 
Special domain units can only be mustered during Intrigue.

The Army/Units of the Organization obeys the commands of the officers and can be deployed outside of intrigue or warfare for narrative purposes.

As a rule of thumb, an army can perform any activity that an organization's officer could perform but which the characters are too high level to bother with, from escorting a diplomat to quelling and uprising of cultists. Usually these things would fall under the **Opertions skill** 

###### **Special units**
Every type of domain (organization) has an action it can use to summon/muster a special unit of rare and powerful creatures. This can be done once pr Intrigue, if the attempt fails, additional attempts can be made during the same Intrigue until successful or the confrontational battle occurs. The special unit disbands and leaves after the battle it is used *(an Intrigue always leads up to a battle and units are mustered to participate in this battle. Defenses are sabotaged or bolstered for this battle as well.)*  The special unit can be mustered again in a new Intrigue. 

A domain can also make use of other special units, by making alliances with other domains and see if the leaders of those are willing to lend their own special units for a battle. This is one reason to do "quests" for other domains (organizations) to gain their goodwill and perhaps the use of their special unit. 

There are also a third type of special units, monsters from the monster book can also in rare cases find themselves on the battlefield as units. 
### Deeper Knowledge on Units

There the following type of units:
Tier 1 
- Infantry
- Infantry levy (zero training), cannot gain experience or gear upgrade and are automatically disbanded after the next battle after they are mustered and must be mustered again. You muster 2 units instead of 1, when mustering levies. 
- Cavalry
- Artillery

Tier 2
- Artillery siege 
- Aerial 

Tier 3
Special units: Dwarven engineers, human hawk riders, elven sharpshooters, orc wyvern riders 
Organization special units 
Extra special units: manticore unit, wraith unit, vrocks 

Tier 4
Dragons 
Giants 
Treants 

Tier 5 
Devil infantry 
Dragons 
Giants 
Elementals 

Army composition has a tier dependency, the highest tier must have one less unit than the tier below it and so on. (3 x Tier one allows 2x Tier two.)

Units have these tiers of experience 
regular 
veteran
elite 
super-elite 

Units can gain these equipment tiers 
light 
medium 
heavy 
super-heavy 

**Experience comes from surviving battles**
• **Regular** units become **veteran** units if they, survive their first battle. Easy!
• **Veteran** units become **elite** units if they survive three more battles. Much harder.
• **Elite** units become **super-elite** units after surviving four more battles (eight total).

**Levies** cannot be improved, as the untrained troops who make up those units are considered to go back to their lives as soon as their task in battle is done.
### Modifying Units
During Intrigue you can use a domain action and the Operations skill to upgrade as many units as are controlled by the officer using the domain action. Upgrades can be made from any level to any lavel you can afford. From light to super-heavy in one go. The costs are cumulative. 

| **Upgrade from…**    | **Cost**                        |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Light to medium      | 500 gp × the tier of the unit   |
| Medium to heavy      | 1,000 gp × the tier of the unit |
| Heavy to super-heavy | 2,000 gp × the tier of the unit |

domain-skills-n-defenses.title: Domain skills n defenses
domain-skills-n-defenses.md:
# Domain Skills N Defenses
Main:
Related: [Organisations MCDM - what is it](#note/organisations-mcdm-what-is-it)

# Skills

During intrigue, each skill can be used to improve a domain’s defense levels or to target the opposed domain and reduce its defense levels. But it’s up to the players and the GM to imagine how this plays out, by translating skill tests and their effects into game terms.
## **Diplomacy:**
*Insight, Persuasion.*

Represent's a domains ability to get what it wants without resorting to war or espionage. Especially Alliances, which is not a mechanical thing, but a narrative of an agreement between two domains. A domain could for instance petition another domain for military aid, which will be in the form of lending a special unit, which each domain has. Only one unit can be provided, so get it before the enemy! Special units on loan return to their owners.

A hostile realm is not the same as a villain realm. A villain realm is actively trying to destroy the pc's. A hostile realm, merely dislike, distrust etc.. the attitudes are: hostile, suspicious, neutral, friendly, allied. 

The main thing an npc realm can aid with according to these rules specifically is the special unit, sitting out a battle (not aiding your enemy). But that does not mean you cannot come up with other forms of aid, retainers, powerful lieutenant or information and so forth. 

## **Espionage:**
*Investigation, Stealth*

Try to learn the secrets of other domains, 
- their plans, 
- their current activites, 
- who they are allied with, 
- learn the makeup of army (which units), 
- which allies will join the battle, 
- determine if they have magical resources or secrets for your Lore skill to research. 
- Usually Espionage targets one of the defenses of a domain (communications, resolve, resources). 

some examples of information to choose to learn:
- The target domain’s current defense scores
- The target domain’s current defense levels
- The target domain’s skill bonuses
- The target domain’s current units
- Another statistic or piece of information, at the GM’s discretion
For instance, knowing what kind of units the opposing organization has mustered can help plan your own mustering or if they are constantly boosting a specific defense maybe it's time to try and sabotage that.

## **Lore:**
*Arcana, History, Religion*

Lore represents  a domain's ability to research both magical and historical knowledge. It is a broad and wide ranging skill, which outside of Intrigue can be used to unlock arcane discoveries, dig up details of forgotten history, discover the existence of lost spells or reveal answers to ancient mysteries.. perhaps.

While Lore is almost limitless, the GM rules what is reasonable and the skill should never be used as a substitute for adventuring. 

A team of npc agents might be sent out to recover the headpiece of the staff of Ra as the PC's quest to find the map room in the hidden well of souls. 

Lore operations is not neccesarily just thumbing through 80 pages in a book. It can include active invistigative operations with agents in the field or getting knowledge in shady ways, perhaps even mystically dangerous ways.

Lore can also be used to learn magical secrets of an opposed domain. Such as supernatural attacks or defenses, or any famous magical items and extraordinary units in their army. 
## **Operations:**
*Associated Character Skills: Athletics, Insight *

Operations represents a domain’s ability to:
- muster new units, as a general rule this doesnt require a test unless GM decides that it can fail.
	- a domain officer can use a domain action during intrigue to muster a new unit under their command. 
	- an officer can control a number of units equal to their proficiency bonus.
	- Units mustered through alliances and diplomacy are controlled by a character but not owned by that character, they return to their npc realm after the battle.
- a domain officer can use a domain action during intrigue to spend gold on Upgrading/Modifying unit equipment: light to medium, medium to heavy, heavy to super heavy. The officer can upgrade as many units as he controls. Upgrading can go from light to superheavy in one upgrade. 
	- alliance units and levies cannot be upgraded
	- upgraded units retain their original tier
- perform many of the basic functions of maintaining a domain. 
- construct fortifications for battlefields, e.g. stone fence, tower, palisade and other fortifications
- This is intended to be a catchall domain skill for any activity the players or GM might think of that doesn’t easily fit into another skill.

**Disbanding Units**

Eventually, a domain will max out the number of units it controls, making it impossible to muster any new units. When this happens, a domain can disband any number of units to free up space
in its army. This isn’t an action, but is simply an order an officer can issue under the umbrella of the Operations skill. The domain does not regain any money spent on equipment upgrades for units that are disbanded.

**Beyond Intrigue**

The Operations domain skill covers many mundane activities outside of intrigue, including building roads or watchtowers, sending out a unit of scouts to explore the local wilderness, and so forth. Anything a domain might reasonably be able to do but which isn’t covered by another domain skill can be accomplished using Operations.

Not only do domain skills allow a domain to do things while the characters are adventuring, they allow the domain to do things outside the scope of adventuring, from research to sabotage to negotiation.
Players are encouraged to be creative with their domain’s skills, the same way players can improvise how they use a character’s abilities and skills. Don’t worry about “doing it right.”
But it’s up to the players and the GM to imagine how this plays out, by translating skill tests and their effects into game terms

You use a domain skill to improve a domain defense.
You use a domain skill to sabotage an opponent domain's defense.
You use a domain skill to put your Organization to other uses outside of intrigue. 

## Lowering a Domain’s Defenses

In the same manner, the players can target a villainous realm in the hopes of lowering that domain’s defense levels. An acting officer picks a skill and one of the opposed domain’s defenses, then describes how they intend to use that skill to compromise the defense. If the scenario makes sense to the GM, the officer rolls a d20, adds the domain skill’s modifier, adds their proficiency bonus if applicable, and compares the result with the enemy realm’s defense score. If the result is equal to or greater than the chosen defense’s score, that defense is lowered one level. If the player rolls a 20 on the check, the chosen defense is lowered two levels. The level of any defense cannot be decreased below -3.

Villainous realms can target the defenses of the heroes’ organization in the same way, with the GM making the decision as to which officer, skill, and specific approach are involved.

*For example, Anna (playing a character named Judge) wants to raise the Communications level of her group’s mercenary company, the Chain of Acheron, using that organization’s Espionage domain skill. She tells the GM: “I want to require all our agents to use only verbal communications, nothing written down, and to use our secret battle language.”

*This is a great idea—but it’s not necessarily easy to implement. The Chain of Acheron has a lot of soldiers, agents, and allies in the city, so there’s no guarantee that these orders will work well enough to make a difference. To make the domain skill test, Anna rolls a d20 and adds the Espionage bonus for Acheron’s Chain. She also adds Judge’s proficiency bonus, since Judge is proficient in Investigation and has not already used their bonus during this intrigue (you may only use proficiency bonus once pr character the entire Intrigue).*
# Defenses

## Communications
This defense is a measure of how rapidly and accurately informations are transmitted between officers and the npc's of the organization. 

Communications directly affects an army's ability to coordinate its activities. 
A high communications (must be bolstered from 0 each intrigue) allows an army to manuever into a better starting deployment. 
Poor or compromised communications lets a domain's enemies know what its officers and agents are doing and can interfere with deployment by false signals & missives. 
This takes the form of repositioning your units on the battlefield, either by your domain or the opposed domain to units being removed from battle. 
## Resolve
This defense measures the commitment the domain's npc's has to its cause. It depends on many factors, including how well the followers understand the domain's cause. The domain by default shares the philosophy of its officers and leaders. 
Resolve directly affects the officers. If everyone working for the domain is committed and engaged, it makes training easier and inspires hope and confidence in victory. The reverse is also true. 
High resolve for a battle means the officers are energized, coordinated and convinced of victory. This grants them benefits in combat against the opposed domain's officers. The reverse is also true. 
This takes the form of advantages/disadvantages, speed increase/decrease.

## Resources
This is a measure of the domain's wealth. Though this defense represents more than money. The resources includes whatever a domain values and collects. Gold, knowledge, secrets or more esoteric things. 
A high Resource affects the gear of the domain's units, granting them improved power or damage. Poor resource affects morale, resembling troops not being fed or armor and weapons in need of repairs.
This takes the form of extra damage, adv. on power tests to disadv. on morale and command test.

warfare-system-round-checklist.title: Warfare system - Round checklist
warfare-system-round-checklist.md:
At the beginning of the round, check for collapsing ranks.

Commanders take turns in initiative order.  
Commanders activate their controlled units on their turn.

During an activation,
the unit regains its reaction.
Then, it takes damage from tokens.  Remove one token of each type.

You have a move, an action, and possible bonus action.

If you attack, you can't move.

If you use a maneuver that requires an action and fail the Command test, you can still simply attack as long as you haven't moved.  

After all commanders have taken their turns, check the point values of each side, if yours is *more than double your opponents', you win. (50%+1)

The round ends.

# Aurilia's HQ Report

- Many people have sought out the headquarters of the Shadow Company, in the hopes of earning money the only way they know how, getting revenge on the goblins, fleeing from authority, creating a new life for themselves or any number of other reasons. The people "making camp" at the Fallen star inn are many and diverse. 
- See Organization Diagram appendix
- I need the Senior Officers to decide how to develop the organization. ( You have 8 points to allocate in either a skill or a defense.)
- Current start skill & defense mod/score is highlighted. 
- Organization skills:  diplomacy, espionage, lore, operations are skills that define how your organization interacts with the world and other organizations. 
	- each skill is the summation of "an entire department in the organization", followers, retainers, experts etc.. 
	- the organizations npc's can mount operations on their own by direction of the senior officers, enabling the organization to do things while the pc's are adventuring as well as doing things that are outside the scope of adventuring. 
- Domain defenses:  communications, resolve, resources, the number on the sheet is the DC score an opposed organization has to beat to sabotage that defense 
	- Defenses also come into play in warfare, during intrigue the organization skills are used to either bolster your own defense or sabotage the opposing organizations defenses 
- Each senior officer takes turn allocating 1 point until there are no points left. 
	- either 1 point in a skill or 1 point in a defense 
	- Blank cells counts as a point allocation, that doesn't improve the modifier or score, in essence making the next modifier/score cost extra points. 
	- See the [Compendium](https://discord.com/channels/487691960447139850/1171173157105827882) for more information on skills and defenses 

# Structuring the Organization
### Chiefs - Department Managers - Junior Officers
These are your contacts in the organization for the various skills and defenses.
They run the day to day as well as plan and/or carry out operations requested by the senior officers. 
Therefore they do not go on adventures with the party as regular retainers. 
Any senior officer can order them around, even though they may have a specific senior officer they answer to.
### Organization Skills
Alright, mighty officers, i have taken the liberty of assigning you to each junior officer. If you want to change any of the assigned Senior officers let me know. 

The junior officers will of cource be instructed to obey orders and commands from ANY senior officer. 
The day to day small matters are reported to your representative Aurilia.
Send missives with orders & commands to me: Aurilia via the [Diplomats pouch](#note/diplomats-pouch) and I will hand them over to the junior officers. 

**Vice-Consul** answers to: [Cedric Belmote](#note/cedric-belmote)
**Spy master** answers to: [Brumor stålfod](#note/brumor-stalfod)
**Chancellor Arcane** answers to: [Anton Keene](#note/anton-keene)
**Castellan** answers to: [Frekka Flammehår](#note/frekka-flammehar)

| **Vice-Consul - diplomacy** - Cedric            | **Spy Master - espionage** - Brumor |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
|                                       |                             |
| **Chancellor Arcane - Lore & Research** - Anton | **Castellan - Operations** - Frekka |
|                                       |                            |

### Organization Warfare / Defenses
**The Master of the Dispatch** answers to **the Arcane Strategist**
**The Vicar**answers to **the Chaplain**. 
**The Quartermaster** answers to **the Master at Arms**. 
But any officer can request tasks of them. 

Day to day small matters, the three junior officers of defense reports to **the Castellan of Operations**. 

| **Master of the dispatch - Communications** - Anton | **Vicar - Resolve** - Brumor |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
|                                           |                 |
| **Quartermaster - Resources** - Frekka              |                              |
|                                          |                              |

- 

- [ ] Senior Officers, assign yourselves as commanders of 1 or more units and give your unit a name. 
- [ ] If you opt for one of the units to be Dwarven heritage, specify this under ancestry. The other two will be human. '
- [ ] You can choose to muster 2 levies instead of an infantry unit. However they will disband 
- An army obeys the commands of an organization’s officers, and can be deployed outside of intrigue or warfare for narrative purposes. As a rule, an army can perform any activity that an organization’s officers could perform but which the characters are too high a level to bother with, from escorting a diplomat to quelling an uprising of cultists.
- The Operations domain skill can be used to resolve tasks an army performs outside of warfare battle.

I will be making extensive notes on [Antero Calaman](#note/antero-calaman)'s advice regarding the operations of an organization and how you can bring it's resources to bear against others or just put it to work for you. 

I will be giving myself a handsome salery for all this paperwork! 

PS. We will be running supply runs to Delios or possibly Bedegaarn as the people that have flocked to your HQ and camped here are putting some strain on the inn's inventory. 
PSS. I have taken the liberty of sending some men to [blackbriar monastery](#note/blackbriar-monastery) to buy some supplies as well, especially their Schnaps.
PSSS. There is a ton of information to absorb from [Antero Calaman](#note/antero-calaman) so im sure there are gaps and holes in what i have written down for you for now. Addendums and Changes are most likely to follow.....

1d4 pr 500 inhabitant +2
Delios: 1000, 2d4 +2 pr type

2d4+2 jewelry = 7
2d4+2 gems = 10
2d4+2 art objects = 6

1 day, 23 items - no more can be sold until the local market changes over time. 
total sell value: 6875

Offer to unload everything all at once, the [Ravenscrest Emporium](#note/ravenscrest-emporium).
They will take everything but at a 50% cut. 
Total sale value: 19.930
This include some items that are too valuable to be sold in this town.

Beskeder til steffen 

1 dag på at sortere og detecte osv. 1 dag på at rende rundt i byen og støve køber op og forhandle bedst mulige priser. 23 items kan blive afsat på denne facon, til en værdi af 7110GP. Jeg har listen over hvilke items og hvilke priser de kan skaffe. Det er muligt at forsøge at "drive a hard bargain" og presse priserne op, men hvis det fejler falder prisen +/- 50%, dette skal gøres individuelt pr item.  Intet er solgt på dette tidspunkt, du har indsamlet tilbud fra vilkårlige købere i byen, butikker eller rejsende. 

Dagen efter bliver Brumor opsøgt af en kvinde ... [Ashley Seidel](#note/ashley-seidel) en associate of the [Ravenscrest Emporium](#note/ravenscrest-emporium).
Hun har hørt at du forsøger at sælge, en hoard, som hun kalder det og dette er en af deres spids kompetancer. De opkøber gerne store mængder med øje for videresalg.
Hun vil gerne tilbyde at købe hele listen, og skal blot bruge et par minutter på lige at skimme indholdet. 

Catchen er at Emporiummet tager en % del og det er sådan at de tjener deres penge. 
Sælger får 50% og Emporiummet tager 50% til vurderings omkostninger, forretnings omkostninger osv og profit. 
Så på bundlinien har de ikke 50% overskud, måske 10-30%.
Tilgengæld kan de købe flere ting og køber uanset værdi af genstandene.
De har "huse" rundt omkring i landet. [Alistair Kingsley](#note/alistair-kingsley) er hendes arbejdsgiver, de er netop landet i byen for en uges tid siden og har skænket byen et badhus som gave og goodwill.
De har købt et hus de er igang med at bygge om og indrette, men Ashley er allerede sat i arbejde med opsøgende køb. 
Der vil i fremtiden også blive afholdt auktioner og lign. Delios er en by i vækst og Magnus Blackthorn som ejer Emporiummet ynder at være til stede så tidligt som muligt når byer vokser sig store og stærke.
Hun tilbyder også en slags bekendtskabsgave/introduktionsgave:
	- Wax to increase leather backpack protection from rain, enough for 1 applications each. (4 jars)
	- 4 Flasks of water repellant oils, to protect your weapons and armor from being attacked by rust in case of bad weather.
